name: Common Sense Tax Team
subject: In 1773...
body:
Peter, a group of fed-up colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor. They weren’t against paying their way. They were against being taken advantage of.
| |
---
Peter,
In 1773, a group of fed-up colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor. They weren’t against paying their way. They were against being taken advantage of. **Sound familiar?** Most folks don’t mind paying their fair share. You believe in a strong military, safe roads, and a country that works. What you mind is paying more than you owe. And year after year, that’s exactly what most hardworking Americans do. **You’ve probably felt it...** A refund that feels like a win, even though it was your money all along.
A tax bill that keeps climbing no matter how carefully you file.
That nagging sense that the people who really know the rules are playing a different game. You’re not imagining it. They are. **Here's what will fix it:** a plan built around your income, your family, and the rules already on the books. That’s what we do at Tru-Fit. Start with our free **Tax Savings Calculator.** Answer a few quick questions, and you’ll see a starting estimate of what you’re overpaying every year. **[Calculate My Savings](https://xtz223.keap-link013.com/v2/click/814794e65d05baec4c654676d89c1464/eJyNkFFrwjAQx7_LPXe2aeuchSFFREqdD2N7lpDeZliahORiddLvvjg2nybs9f6_-x3_OwOh5pqaDio40meeF5CAQyGtRE1Lo4mL7zSflqxgCSipP9bOBAvV-c_lK3AZM5ZlZQJ0shiZl-d62Tbb9W7TbNuIWu7ikX-J5tns4epZPdXNBsbxphh7SatDdHuoyAW8VOpkrEWvTkV-T2R9labDMExi_iaJ-HEiTJ96fpD63d8JrkRQnIxbBOp33gQn8BF7LlX0c2tRdz_fafH0e0V6H7CrYyU2m5dFydj0fvwCH2p1cgEGCtyNY01WeI6aQTQghubp)** Keep in mind, that’s only the beginning. When we dig in and build out a full game plan, we usually find about three times what the calculator shows. Once you see your results, a calendar will come up so you can book a game plan call with my team. That’s where we show you exactly how to capture those savings before December 31. [Go straight to the calendar here.](https://xtz223.keap-link013.com/v2/click/be188ced28d82674e40d4df55dc2a977/eJyNkMFqwzAQRP9lz1Zs2U7S-GZCCMZpDqU9F2ErrYgsCWkV4gb_e9elzamFXkdPb5i9AUojDDY9VHDFjzwvIAEvO-WUNLi1BkX39ZovS17wBLQy57230UF1-_XzHZhjzrNslQCOThLz_FRv2-a4fz00x5ZQJzyV_Eu0ydYPd8_usW4OME1_iuWgcHchd4AKfZTzpF7RLHzxmvh3RBeqNO2ElqbX46KzQ4onFFenhTHKvKWjjZ51MaAdGOUsiAvFgdE5lDVs5qhIOEeC7zO1cvypUyFE2de0ja83ZVFyvlxNn1GQeI8BtguhvmMoVFb3kxACsfs9vQ==) There's still time before the end of the year, but we're closing in. The founders fought for the right to keep what’s theirs. The least we can do is stop handing it over by accident. Rob Gill The Tru-Fit Tax Team

Hello, and thank you for taking the time to read this email. This message is part of an ongoing conversation between us, and I want to take a moment to ensure you have full transparency about why you received this message, how your information is handled, and what to expect from future emails. Why You’re Receiving This Email You’re receiving this email because at some point, you opted in to receive updates, news, or information on a specific topic we’ve previously discussed or shared. Whether it was through a subscription, a form submission, or another form of communication, your information was shared willingly, and we respect your decision to connect with us. If you’re wondering about the nature of our correspondence, rest assured that we aim to keep all emails relevant, timely, and free from unnecessary clutter. This includes respecting your inbox and refraining from sending irrelevant messages. Your Privacy is Important We value your trust and take your privacy very seriously. The information you provide is securely stored and never shared, sold, or used outside the purpose for which you provided it. If you ever want to review how we handle your data, feel free to contact us directly. Transparency is our priority, and we’re happy to address any questions you might have. You are always in control of the information you share. If you feel that any part of your subscription or interaction needs clarification, let us know. We’re here to provide accurate answers and ensure your satisfaction. How to Unsubscribe or Manage Your Preferences We understand that everyone’s inbox is different. If you ever find our emails no longer relevant, there’s no hard feelings. You can easily manage your email preferences or unsubscribe using the link provided below. By clicking the unsubscribe link, you’ll be taken to a page where you can either adjust your communication preferences (such as receiving fewer emails or only on specific topics) or completely remove yourself from our list. The process is straightforward, and any changes will take effect promptly. We don’t use tricks or gimmicks to keep you subscribed. Our priority is to ensure that our emails add value to your day, and if they don’t, we respect your decision to part ways. Accessibility and Communication If you have any trouble accessing the unsubscribe page, managing preferences, or understanding why you’re receiving this email, you can reach out directly to our support team at taxteam@tftaxplanning.com. We aim to provide a response within a reasonable time frame and address your concerns effectively. Our communication is designed to be as inclusive as possible, but we know there’s always room for improvement. If you have any feedback on how we can make our emails more accessible or relevant, please don’t hesitate to share. A Commitment to Non-Intrusive Emails We aim to create a non-intrusive communication experience. This means we won’t overwhelm your inbox with excessive messages, and we work hard to ensure our content remains clear and concise. The purpose of this email is to stay connected with you and provide updates or information that we believe is meaningful. If we ever fail to meet these standards, we encourage you to let us know. Feedback, whether positive or constructive, is always appreciated. Your thoughts help us understand how we can do better and improve our communication approach. While we cannot guarantee every suggestion will be implemented, we will take the time to carefully review and consider your input. Contact Information If you’d like to get in touch with us outside of managing your preferences, here’s how you can reach us: Email: taxteam@tftaxplanning.com
Phone: (732) 558-1353
Mailing Address: 100 Bingham ave
Rumson, NJ 07760 We strive to ensure all communication channels are open and readily available to you. Whether it’s a question, comment, or concern, our team is ready to assist. Legal Information We comply with all applicable laws and regulations regarding email communication. This includes adhering to anti-spam laws and maintaining the highest standards for consent-based communication. Your trust matters, and we work diligently to ensure every email you receive meets these requirements. If you need further clarification on our compliance policies or legal obligations, please feel free to ask. Transparency and accountability are central to our communication strategy, and we’re happy to provide additional details if needed. A Final Note Emails are one of the many ways we stay connected, but we understand they aren’t perfect for everyone. If there’s another way you’d prefer to communicate or stay updated, let us know. Whether it’s through social media, a direct call, or another channel, we’re open to finding the most effective way to share information with you. We want to emphasize that our goal is never to disrupt or clutter your inbox. Every email sent is intended to provide value, and we genuinely appreciate your time and attention. Thank you for allowing us to stay in touch with you. This footer was designed to ensure transparency, provide essential information, and give you full control over your communication preferences. We hope it meets your expectations, but if there’s anything you’d like to see improved, we’re always here to listen.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/cfad7424-7bd5-426a-b2d5-fccd5faf5c24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Members of the Novaya Gazeta staff gather outside the daily's offices in Moscow, Russia, on November 9, 2026. Photo by Tatyana Makeyeva/AFP via Getty Images.
**Tuesday, November 10, 2026 - **
_**Iran:** Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says. Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over." GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait. France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers._
_**Palestine:** Three killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza on Tuesday. Israeli settlers and soldiers simultaneously raid Beita, in occupied West Bank. Settlers attack Palestinian farmers. Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements. Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration._
_**Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a kill one person. Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days. Saudi pipeline targeted._
_**Lebanon:** Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire._
_**U.S.:** Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work. Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race. California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax." Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas' Big Bend region. Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms. Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns. Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says hasn't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman. TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role._
_**International:** Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities. France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests. Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orban. 2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad. Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria. South African police arrest nine foreign nationals suspected of trying to join Russia's war on Ukraine. Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office. Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela. Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.UM4QPFCy416YSFRRr2jkF50j2SDHu0msdHcisY9XD0E?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=224318707)
* * *
# Iran
* **Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says:** The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Crops (IRGC) said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using what it said was an "unauthorised route."
* In a statement, the IRGC said, "One of these vessels, a supertanker, hit a naval mine and exploded, and the second tanker, which was under the protection of the US aggressor's fighter jets and was attempting to secretly pass through the illegal route, had an accident and was stopped in its place with a terrible fire."
* **Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over": **President Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/aef60a2d-4ab3-489c-8904-b952bfb707c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that the Iran war is "militarily effectively over," while signaling that the U.S. blockade would continue. Trump's announcement follows talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani in Washington, DC.
* Speaking at a news conference, Trump said "Iran militarily is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo, and we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbors." He added, "We just had, just in case, another aircraft carrier. We have many. Sailing over and just arriving in the Middle East, so we have three. And they're all locked and loaded, and hopefully we don't have to use them."
* In a phone interview with C-SPAN on Monday, Trump also claimed that Iran wanted to reach an agreement with Washington. "They want to make a deal. They don't say that, you know, publicly," he said. "In speaking with Qatar--as you know, the prime minister was in the Oval Office today--in speaking to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait ... they'd rather do it this way rather than another hit, which would be approximately five times bigger than the first hit."
* Iranian Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei denied Trump's claims that Iran was seeking a deal. "The war on Iran has already wrecked the U.S. government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER," Rezaei wrote in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/1b78de7c-e811-4857-9d05-84632d3e651b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X.
* **GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait:** Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states approved the establishment of an advanced headquarters for their unified military command in Kuwait and the deployment of forces to the facility, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said in a statement.
* "These directives reflect a firm Gulf commitment to safeguarding the security and sovereignty of the GCC states and strengthening their ability to confront common threats," Albudaiwi added.
* **France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers:** On Monday, France [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/7757a35e-af5a-4e52-b081-5e4ff810fc93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran of orchestrating cyberattacks that knocked out hundreds of commercial refrigerators and freezers at French supermarkets in October. French officials said that there would be "consequences" for the attack. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said that he summoned the Iranian ambassador and threatened further European Union sanctions against Iran. On October 11, a series of hacks targeted 700 commercial sites in France, sparking at least 15 fires. A second series of hacks this month hit more than 100 European establishments, including French blood-bank refrigerators.

# Palestine
* **Three killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza on Tuesday:** Two Palestinians were killed, including a child, and several people were wounded in an Israeli air strike on a shelter in the Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. Separately, a Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis.
* Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed one Palestinian and injured 16 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered from under the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,645 killed and 175,978 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,614 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,849, while 850 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli settlers and soldiers simultaneously raid Beita, in occupied West Bank:** On Monday, dozens of Israeli settlers [stormed](https://substack.com/redirect/2bed355e-fb7d-48ce-90df-b4955cb71992?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an industrial zone in Beita, south of Nablus, and set fire to three bulldozers, several other vehicles, and equipment belonging to stone-cutting workshops, WAFA reported. Israeli forces raided the town simultaneously.
* Settlers have repeatedly attacked Beita's industrial zone, burning facilities and vehicles and opening fire on Palestinians.
* Settler attacks across the occupied West Bank more than doubled in October to 1,369, with 353 in the Nablus governorate alone, according to the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.
* **Settlers attack Palestinian farmers:** Israeli settlers blocked Palestinian farmers from reaching their olive groves near Silwad, east of Ramallah, on Monday.
* Settlers also attacked farmers picking olives near the town's cemetery and forced them off their land, WAFA reported.
* **Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements:** The United Kingdom has awarded 10.7 million pounds (around $14.4 million) in new public contracts to companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite the British government's recent pledge to punish companies that profit from settlement activity, an Al Jazeera [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/9a32f608-dce5-49d6-baf0-1a87f26db43d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found. The contracts were publicized following UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in September. At the time, the UK government said it would take action against companies aiding settlement expansion.
* **Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration:** A petition on the UK Parliament's website that [calls](https://substack.com/redirect/5987e0b2-ddd1-49d3-9757-d4dd736a9c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a public investigation into British government complicity in the Gaza genocide passed 100,000 signatures on Monday, requiring Parliament to formally consider the measure. The petition specifically demands that the inquiry empower investigators to question government ministers and officials, and to uncover "the sale, supply, or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft, and Royal Air Force bases" in support of the genocide. The petition was launched by Jennifer Forbes, a member of Your Party, the left-wing party headed in Parliament by Jeremy Corbyn. In 2024, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK created an air bridge supporting Israel's war, and that UK firms supplied jet parts to the Israeli military.

# Yemen
* **Saudi airstrikes on Sana 'a kill one person: **A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a gas station in Sana'a on Tuesday, killing one person and injuring three others, according to the spokesperson for the health ministry in Sana'a.
* Another Saudi-coalition airstrike targeted an oil company building in the capital, injuring at least six people, causing "extensive damage" to nearby homes and shops.
* Ansarallah said that Saudi-led strikes targeted sites in several governorates on Monday and Tuesday, including Hodeidah and Saada.
* **Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days:** At least 33 civilians have been killed and 58 others wounded in attacks by Ansarallah in the governorate of Taiz over the past 73 hours, the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms said on Monday.
* The rights group documented 133 violations against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including 216 projectiles fired at residential areas.
* The group also blamed Ansarallah for an attack on a market in Al-Waziiya district on Friday, which it said killed at least 30 people and wounded 45 others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack.
* **Saudi pipeline targeted:** Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region was "targeted" on Monday, sparking a "limited fire" that was quickly extinguished, the Saudi Energy Ministry said. There were no casualties, and oil operations continued. The ministry did not say who carried out the attack, and no group claimed responsibility for it as of Monday night.
* Separately, satellite images on November 8 show "possible signs of damage" at Pumping Station 8 along the pipeline, according to the satellite-imagery firm Soar Atlas. The roughly 1,200 km pipeline carries about 4 million barrels a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

# Lebanon
* **Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire:** Israeli fighter jets attacked the town of Qantara on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera. Footage shows smoke billowing at the scene. Israeli forces also fired toward the outskirts of the town of Chaqra, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The towns of al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun were also targeted by Israeli artillery.

# U.S. News
* **Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work: Derek Utley,** a co-founder of the digital strategy firm X Strategies, filed a lawsuit in Florida on Monday [accusing](https://substack.com/redirect/341c30db-babf-4263-a9d8-1c7bdf9f0293?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**** his former partner, **Alex Bruesewitz** ,**** of accepting $500,000 from "individuals associated with Qatar," arguing that he violated federal law by failing to disclose the payments. Bruesewitz, who continues to run X Strategies after an acrimonious split with Utley, worked as an aide on President Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and continues to work on behalf of Republican causes and candidates. He is a senior adviser to President Trump's primary leadership PAC, Never Surrender. In that work, he runs the popular social-media accounts @TrumpWarRoom and @TeamTrump. Through a lawyer, Bruesewitz denied the claims in Utley's complaint.
* **Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race:** Mississippi's**** Democratic Senate candidate **Scott Colom** [remains](https://substack.com/redirect/59afd5bb-b45a-4a00-957b-ee7a19a9d110?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ahead of incumbent Republican Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith** , leading by 2,574 votes, according to a Monday tally from the Associated Press. Mississippi election officials have until Tuesday to count provisional (affidavit) ballots and receive postmarked absentee ballots, and all 82 counties have until Friday to certify their results. Mississippi Secretary of State **Michael Watson** said that about 2,800 absentee ballots still need to be counted, most of which are from the Democrat-leaning counties of Hinds and Holmes. Mississippi does not have a mechanism for an automatic vote recount, meaning that a losing candidate must file a lawsuit to gain one.
* **California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax": **California voters [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/5337f722-acd3-43fd-af5e-24d9f635dafc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Proposition 40, a ballot proposition that would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on residents whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, the AP reported on Monday. If it had passed, the taxed money would have supplemented the $100 billion that California is projected to lose as a result of federal healthcare cuts over the next five years. Organized opposition to the proposition was widespread. Google co-founder **Sergey Brin** donated more than $100 million to a PAC opposed to the proposition. Gov. **Gavin Newsom** , a possible 2028 presidential candidate, opposed it, as did Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association. Sen. **Bernie Sanders**(D-Vt.)**** campaigned for it. The "Yes on 40" campaign said that it may return the measure to the ballot in 2028.
* **Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas ' Big Bend region: **The Supreme Court [lifted](https://substack.com/redirect/11ac81d7-6945-435f-b656-4a7f0d822165?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a federal judge's recent halt on construction in Texas' Big Bend region on Monday, allowing the Trump administration to move forward with its planned expansion of border security and surveillance measures along a roughly 500-mile stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border. A legal challenge to the project is still wending its way through the courts. Only Justice **Ketanji Brown Jackson** noted her dissent to Monday's decision. The plaintiffs in the ongoing case against the project include an environmental group, local preservationists, a river guide, and a landowner. The Trump administration previously dropped plans for a wall inside Big Bend National Park, opting instead for the construction of patrol roads, vehicle barriers, and surveillance infrastructure.
* **Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms:** The Senate voted to formally [take up](https://substack.com/redirect/f5995f19-908b-459e-846d-1cd2c71416be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a bill on Monday that would streamline environmental permitting for data centers. The legislation would shorten approval timelines for large, energy-intensive projects, while requiring owners of data centers to pay for the energy they use. The bill was negotiated before the election by Republican Sens. **Shelley Moore Capito**(W. Va.) and **Mike Lee** (Utah), and Democratic Sens. **Martin Heinrich** (N.M.) and **Sheldon Whitehouse**(R.I.). Trump expressed support for the bill in a post on social media on Sunday. Environmental groups like the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation have strongly opposed its passage.
* **Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns: Brett Shumate** , the head of the Justice Department's civil division, [resigned](https://substack.com/redirect/a49814fa-2c37-48ca-b05d-87a5975aaf69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday.**** The civil division represents the government in most litigation, defending federal policies and presidential actions, and handling fraud and immigration enforcement cases. Shumate is the latest DOJ departure since the midterms. Other DOJ officials who have recently resigned include Civil Rights Division chief **Harmeet Dhillon** , National Security Division head **John Eisenberg,** and veteran litigator **Henry Whitaker** , an aide to Attorney General **Todd Blanche**.
* **Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker: **House Minority Leader **Hakeem Jeffries**(N.Y.) [told](https://substack.com/redirect/d4029121-f29d-40a3-99aa-e469e2f3f311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters on Monday that he is "confident" he will be elected speaker of the House in January. He added that the Democratic Caucus will meet next Wednesday to choose its leader. To win the election for speaker, he will need to reach 218 votes. Democrats are expected to hold 254 seats in the next Congress. Reps.-elect **Darializa Avila Chevalier**(D-N.Y.) and **Melat Kiros** (D-Colo.) have expressed reluctance to support Jeffries. Chevalier said that she would prefer a speaker who will fight for "working-class people [and] Medicare for All." Kiros said that she would not vote for a speaker who accepts corporate PAC money, as Jeffries does. Other incoming Democratic representatives, including **Richard Ojeda** (N.C.) and **Katy Padilla Stout** (Texas), declined to endorse Jeffries. A public petition [urging](https://substack.com/redirect/3358e8fb-031f-44a0-9daf-5a311b0a087b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Jeffries to step aside has reached over 1 million signatures.
* **Sen. Chris Van Hollen says hasn 't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader: **Maryland Democrat Sen. **Chris Van Hollen** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/d7a06a34-0b6f-42a4-8037-2e62dd20b4ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that the party "shouldn't have a coronation" for majority leader, and that he "hasn't shut the door" to a possible run for the position. Sen. **Chuck Schumer** , leader of the Democratic Senate Caucus since 2017, is widely expected to win enough support to become Senate majority leader in a closed-door vote in early December. Sen. **Elissa Slotkin** , who met with Van Hollen on Monday and hasn't ruled out her own run for the leadership role, said that she won't vote for a candidate who cannot articulate "a plan" for Democrats, especially for the first 100 days of the new Congress.
* **Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman: Ahmed Moor** , a 42-year-old Palestinian American writer and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/e7ae4323-eeaf-46af-99ce-17d762fd9d0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he will challenge Sen. **John Fetterman** (D-Penn.) in the 2028 primary. Fetterman is among Israel's most vociferous defenders in the Democratic Party, and he votes in alignment with the Trump agenda [more frequently](https://substack.com/redirect/1e7d0580-224c-4b8f-9e08-452639ec455c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than any other Democratic legislator. Moor said that he is "not really running against Fetterman" but "for good government" and "the rule of law."
* **TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role:** The White House is attempting to appoint **Christopher Mufarrige** to the vacant Republican commissioner's seat on the Federal Trade Commission, The American Prospect [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/9fa9c790-e55d-4c60-9760-15d9e8dfa0fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). His nomination could be announced during a hearing of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee on Tuesday. Mufarrige ran a "buy here, pay here" used-car business in Texas called CNJ Auto Finance for three years in the late 2000s. Such businesses have been criticized for predatory tactics like imposing high interest rates on consumers who have poor credit, targeting consumers who publicly file for bankruptcy, and rapidly repossessing vehicles if consumers default on their loans. Mufarrige's firm was unsuccessfully sued twice, once for taking vehicles without proper payment and another time for failure to pay property taxes. TAP's full report is available [here](https://substack.com/redirect/9fa9c790-e55d-4c60-9760-15d9e8dfa0fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

# Other International News
* **Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities:** The Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta [held](https://substack.com/redirect/bf1361b5-8dc4-4ab8-827d-1d0da1c1a486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its last editorial meeting on Monday and closed its Moscow newsroom. It announced in October that it was being forced to shut down after the government designated it a "foreign agent," and cut its access to the Russian banking system. Authorities arrested an editor at the paper, Oleg Roldugin, in April, and last month they searched the home of editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov and questioned him. UN rights chief Volker Turk called Russia's crackdown on the publication "yet another devastating blow for remaining independent media" in the country. Novaya Gazeta was co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev and funded with money from his Nobel Peace Prize. The paper was one of the few outlets that openly criticized Russia's war in Ukraine.
* **France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests:** France will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% on December 1, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/7757a35e-af5a-4e52-b081-5e4ff810fc93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday, expediting an increase that was scheduled for January 2027. The increase raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros ($27), from 1,477.93 euros ($1,656) to 1,502 euros ($1,683). Lecornu told reporters this was "the second-largest rise in 20 years" and "not merely symbolic." It falls short of trade unions' demands, however. The French Democratic Confederation of Labour wants a raise of at least 100 euros, and the General Confederation of Labour has demanded a raise of about 150 euros. CGT head Sophie Binet called Monday's raise "crumbs."
* **Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orb an: **Hungarian police [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/173a2520-b0db-4889-9dcd-ae18322dcf7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Viktor Orban's younger brother Aron on Monday, on suspicion of "people smuggling" and other offenses, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban wrote on X that he was "the real target" of the arrest. A 2025 investigation by the news site Telex linked Aron Orban and others to an alleged scheme involving visas for foreign guest workers. Magyar, who won the premiership in a landslide election in April, promised to investigate his predecessor's alleged corruption and abuse of power.
* **2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad:** A harvest failure, insufficient rainfall, and the ongoing civil war have [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/d0375c5c-485c-47e6-9a34-81b298b37595?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 2,510 people to flee Darfur for Chad, the Sudan Tribune reported. Adam Rijal, a spokesperson for the General Coordination of Displaced Persons and Refugees, said that living conditions in Darfur are rapidly deteriorating. He said that the region desperately needs a surge in all kinds of aid--food, water, and medicine.
* **Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria:** Gunmen [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/8464131e-15ce-40d2-821b-bbbc8b0dd9ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a local security volunteer and 10 of his relatives in an attack in Nigeria's northwestern Zamfara state over the weekend, torching his house and abducting a further 13 relatives, Reuters reported. A police official said that the security guard, a member of a government-backed vigilante group, had helped state security forces fend off gang incursions in the area, leading the "bandits" to consider him "an obstacle to their activities." Security forces have been deployed to secure the hostages' release. Armed gangs have long raided villages in northwestern Nigeria, killing residents, abducting people for ransom, and looting homes.
* **South African police arrest nine foreign nationals suspected of trying to join Russia 's war on Ukraine:** South African police [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/0cd6fd23-0e29-4cb9-95c7-b876d81ffaa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nine young men, ages 20 to 26, at Johannesburg's OR Tambo Airport on Sunday night, accusing them of seeking to fight in Russia's war in Ukraine. The arrests follow an investigation involving Interpol and local agencies. South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act bars mercenary activity, recruitment, and training. The arrests come amid concern that Africans, Asians, and South Americans are being lured to Russia with civilian job offers and forced into combat in Ukraine.
* **Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office:** Paraguayan**** prosecutors [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/28f02d3c-4493-4fb0-b0ed-aa2b20cad9e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the digital bank Ueno's brokerage arm on Monday. The raid is part of a widening probe into Ueno, a huge bank whose collapse led to the resignation of Santiago Peña from the presidency last week. Following the raid, prosecutors shared images of ripped-up documents, including fragments of what appeared to be due-diligence reports and emails.
* Separately, Paraguay's Congress approved President Pedro Alliana's nomination of economist Jorge Schreiner to replace former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Tuesday. It also named the former banking regulator Fernando Rivarola, who warned the public about Ueno in a July report, to the board of the central bank. Like the former president Peña, Carvallo has business ties to Ueno. Both men were recently charged with breach of trust and administration and are in pretrial detention.
* **Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela:** ExxonMobil [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/ec1db7fa-a785-4cd7-8340-b829c62382d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that it drafted a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela. The agreement is nonbinding, which allows Exxon to hedge its bets. The company said that "any future investment would require stable policies, clear regulations, strong investment protections and competitive returns." The deal is a symbolic win for Trump and a reversal of Exxon Mobil's position in January, when CEO Darren Woods called Venezuela "uninvestable." Venezuela has twice seized Exxon's assets in the country.
* **Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific: **On Tuesday, Taiwanese**** Defense Minister Wellington Koo [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/617c06a2-1975-4142-b1d7-6d2f697dee5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) China of conducting "area denial" drills in the Western Pacific. Koo told reporters that China used its Liaoning carrier group and other naval formations in the process. "Anti-access area denial" is a military tactic designed to deter outside forces from intervening in conflict. Last week, Taiwan's security chief Joseph Wu said that more than 100 Chinese naval and Coast Guard ships were operating in the South China Sea and in the Pacific, and the defense ministry reported a large rise in Chinese aircraft in the area. China did not respond to Tuesday's accusations, though its defense ministry said last month that the Liaoning carrier group's trainings are scheduled annually and are not aimed at any country.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Two tankers on fire in Hormuz after using "unauthorised route," IRGC says: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Crops (IRGC) said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using what it said was an "unauthorised route." In a statement, the IRGC said, "One of these vessels, a supertanker, hit a naval mine and exploded, and the second tanker, which was under the protection of the US aggressor's fighter jets and was attempting to secretly pass through the illegal route, had an accident and was stopped in its place with a terrible fire." Trump says Iran war "militarily is effectively over": President Donald Trump on Monday that the Iran war is "militarily effectively over," while signaling that the U.S. blockade would continue. Trump's announcement follows talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani in Washington, DC. Speaking at a news conference, Trump said "Iran militarily is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo, and we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbors." He added, "We just had, just in case, another aircraft carrier. We have many. Sailing over and just arriving in the Middle East, so we have three. And they're all locked and loaded, and hopefully we don't have to use them." In a phone interview with C-SPAN on Monday, Trump also claimed that Iran wanted to reach an agreement with Washington. "They want to make a deal. They don't say that, you know, publicly," he said. "In speaking with Qatar--as you know, the prime minister was in the Oval Office today--in speaking to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait ... they'd rather do it this way rather than another hit, which would be approximately five times bigger than the first hit." Iranian Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei denied Trump's claims that Iran was seeking a deal. "The war on Iran has already wrecked the U.S. government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER," Rezaei wrote in a on X. GCC establishes military HQ in Kuwait: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states approved the establishment of an advanced headquarters for their unified military command in Kuwait and the deployment of forces to the facility, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said in a statement. "These directives reflect a firm Gulf commitment to safeguarding the security and sovereignty of the GCC states and strengthening their ability to confront common threats," Albudaiwi added. France accuses IRGC of October cyberattacks on refrigerators and freezers: On Monday, France Iran of orchestrating cyberattacks that knocked out hundreds of commercial refrigerators and freezers at French supermarkets in October. French officials said that there would be "consequences" for the attack. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said that he summoned the Iranian ambassador and threatened further European Union sanctions against Iran. On October 11, a series of hacks targeted 700 commercial sites in France, sparking at least 15 fires. A second series of hacks this month hit more than 100 European establishments, including French blood-bank refrigerators. Palestine Three killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza on Tuesday: Two Palestinians were killed, including a child, and several people were wounded in an Israeli air strike on a shelter in the Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. Separately, a Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis. Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed one Palestinian and injured 16 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered from under the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,645 killed and 175,978 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,614 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,849, while 850 bodies have been recovered. Israeli settlers and soldiers simultaneously raid Beita, in occupied West Bank: On Monday, dozens of Israeli settlers an industrial zone in Beita, south of Nablus, and set fire to three bulldozers, several other vehicles, and equipment belonging to stone-cutting workshops, WAFA reported. Israeli forces raided the town simultaneously. Settlers have repeatedly attacked Beita's industrial zone, burning facilities and vehicles and opening fire on Palestinians. Settler attacks across the occupied West Bank more than doubled in October to 1,369, with 353 in the Nablus governorate alone, according to the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission. Settlers attack Palestinian farmers: Israeli settlers blocked Palestinian farmers from reaching their olive groves near Silwad, east of Ramallah, on Monday. Settlers also attacked farmers picking olives near the town's cemetery and forced them off their land, WAFA reported. Al Jazeera: UK grants contracts to companies linked to Israeli settlements: The United Kingdom has awarded 10.7 million pounds (around $14.4 million) in new public contracts to companies with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite the British government's recent pledge to punish companies that profit from settlement activity, an Al Jazeera found. The contracts were publicized following UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in September. At the time, the UK government said it would take action against companies aiding settlement expansion. Petition for public inquiry into UK complicity in Gaza genocide passes 100,000 signatures, triggering parliamentary consideration: A petition on the UK Parliament's website that for a public investigation into British government complicity in the Gaza genocide passed 100,000 signatures on Monday, requiring Parliament to formally consider the measure. The petition specifically demands that the inquiry empower investigators to question government ministers and officials, and to uncover "the sale, supply, or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft, and Royal Air Force bases" in support of the genocide. The petition was launched by Jennifer Forbes, a member of Your Party, the left-wing party headed in Parliament by Jeremy Corbyn. In 2024, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK created an air bridge supporting Israel's war, and that UK firms supplied jet parts to the Israeli military. Yemen Saudi airstrikes on Sana 'a kill one person: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a gas station in Sana'a on Tuesday, killing one person and injuring three others, according to the spokesperson for the health ministry in Sana'a. Another Saudi-coalition airstrike targeted an oil company building in the capital, injuring at least six people, causing "extensive damage" to nearby homes and shops. Ansarallah said that Saudi-led strikes targeted sites in several governorates on Monday and Tuesday, including Hodeidah and Saada. Yemeni rights group: Over 30 killed in Ansarallah attacks in Taiz over three days: At least 33 civilians have been killed and 58 others wounded in attacks by Ansarallah in the governorate of Taiz over the past 73 hours, the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms said on Monday. The rights group documented 133 violations against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including 216 projectiles fired at residential areas. The group also blamed Ansarallah for an attack on a market in Al-Waziiya district on Friday, which it said killed at least 30 people and wounded 45 others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack. Saudi pipeline targeted: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region was "targeted" on Monday, sparking a "limited fire" that was quickly extinguished, the Saudi Energy Ministry said. There were no casualties, and oil operations continued. The ministry did not say who carried out the attack, and no group claimed responsibility for it as of Monday night. Separately, satellite images on November 8 show "possible signs of damage" at Pumping Station 8 along the pipeline, according to the satellite-imagery firm Soar Atlas. The roughly 1,200 km pipeline carries about 4 million barrels a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Lebanon Israel attacks Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire: Israeli fighter jets attacked the town of Qantara on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera. Footage shows smoke billowing at the scene. Israeli forces also fired toward the outskirts of the town of Chaqra, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The towns of al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun were also targeted by Israeli artillery. U.S. News Trump social-media strategist accused of unregistered Qatar work: Derek Utley, a co-founder of the digital strategy firm X Strategies, filed a lawsuit in Florida on Monday ** his former partner, Alex Bruesewitz , of accepting $500,000 from "individuals associated with Qatar," arguing that he violated federal law by failing to disclose the payments. Bruesewitz, who continues to run X Strategies after an acrimonious split with Utley, worked as an aide on President Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and continues to work on behalf of Republican causes and candidates. He is a senior adviser to President Trump's primary leadership PAC, Never Surrender. In that work, he runs the popular social-media accounts @TrumpWarRoom and @TeamTrump. Through a lawyer, Bruesewitz denied the claims in Utley's complaint. Democrat Scott Colom maintains lead in Mississippi Senate race: Mississippi's** Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom ahead of incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith , leading by 2,574 votes, according to a Monday tally from the Associated Press. Mississippi election officials have until Tuesday to count provisional (affidavit) ballots and receive postmarked absentee ballots, and all 82 counties have until Friday to certify their results. Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson said that about 2,800 absentee ballots still need to be counted, most of which are from the Democrat-leaning counties of Hinds and Holmes. Mississippi does not have a mechanism for an automatic vote recount, meaning that a losing candidate must file a lawsuit to gain one. California voters reject proposed "billionaire tax": California voters Proposition 40, a ballot proposition that would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on residents whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, the AP reported on Monday. If it had passed, the taxed money would have supplemented the $100 billion that California is projected to lose as a result of federal healthcare cuts over the next five years. Organized opposition to the proposition was widespread. Google co-founder Sergey Brin donated more than $100 million to a PAC opposed to the proposition. Gov. Gavin Newsom , a possible 2028 presidential candidate, opposed it, as did Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association. Sen. Bernie Sanders(D-Vt.)** campaigned for it. The "Yes on 40" campaign said that it may return the measure to the ballot in 2028. Supreme Court clears the way for border construction in Texas ' Big Bend region: The Supreme Court a federal judge's recent halt on construction in Texas' Big Bend region on Monday, allowing the Trump administration to move forward with its planned expansion of border security and surveillance measures along a roughly 500-mile stretch of the U.S.-Mexico border. A legal challenge to the project is still wending its way through the courts. Only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson noted her dissent to Monday's decision. The plaintiffs in the ongoing case against the project include an environmental group, local preservationists, a river guide, and a landowner. The Trump administration previously dropped plans for a wall inside Big Bend National Park, opting instead for the construction of patrol roads, vehicle barriers, and surveillance infrastructure. Senate facilitates data-center permitting in first legislation advanced since midterms: The Senate voted to formally a bill on Monday that would streamline environmental permitting for data centers. The legislation would shorten approval timelines for large, energy-intensive projects, while requiring owners of data centers to pay for the energy they use. The bill was negotiated before the election by Republican Sens. Shelley Moore Capito(W. Va.) and Mike Lee (Utah), and Democratic Sens. Martin Heinrich (N.M.) and Sheldon Whitehouse(R.I.). Trump expressed support for the bill in a post on social media on Sunday. Environmental groups like the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation have strongly opposed its passage. Another ranking DOJ attorney resigns: Brett Shumate , the head of the Justice Department's civil division, on Monday.** The civil division represents the government in most litigation, defending federal policies and presidential actions, and handling fraud and immigration enforcement cases. Shumate is the latest DOJ departure since the midterms. Other DOJ officials who have recently resigned include Civil Rights Division chief Harmeet Dhillon , National Security Division head John Eisenberg, and veteran litigator Henry Whitaker , an aide to Attorney General Todd Blanche. Despite increasing Dem discontent, Jeffries says he is "confident" he will be elected House speaker: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries(N.Y.) reporters on Monday that he is "confident" he will be elected speaker of the House in January. He added that the Democratic Caucus will meet next Wednesday to choose its leader. To win the election for speaker, he will need to reach 218 votes. Democrats are expected to hold 254 seats in the next Congress. Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier(D-N.Y.) and Melat Kiros (D-Colo.) have expressed reluctance to support Jeffries. Chevalier said that she would prefer a speaker who will fight for "working-class people [and] Medicare for All." Kiros said that she would not vote for a speaker who accepts corporate PAC money, as Jeffries does. Other incoming Democratic representatives, including Richard Ojeda (N.C.) and Katy Padilla Stout (Texas), declined to endorse Jeffries. A public petition Jeffries to step aside has reached over 1 million signatures. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says hasn 't ruled out challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader: Maryland Democrat Sen. Chris Van Hollen on Monday that the party "shouldn't have a coronation" for majority leader, and that he "hasn't shut the door" to a possible run for the position. Sen. Chuck Schumer , leader of the Democratic Senate Caucus since 2017, is widely expected to win enough support to become Senate majority leader in a closed-door vote in early December. Sen. Elissa Slotkin , who met with Van Hollen on Monday and hasn't ruled out her own run for the leadership role, said that she won't vote for a candidate who cannot articulate "a plan" for Democrats, especially for the first 100 days of the new Congress. Palestinian socialist Ahmed Moor announces 2028 primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman: Ahmed Moor , a 42-year-old Palestinian American writer and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, that he will challenge Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) in the 2028 primary. Fetterman is among Israel's most vociferous defenders in the Democratic Party, and he votes in alignment with the Trump agenda than any other Democratic legislator. Moor said that he is "not really running against Fetterman" but "for good government" and "the rule of law." TAP: Trump administration looks to install former subprime autolender in key regulatory role: The White House is attempting to appoint Christopher Mufarrige to the vacant Republican commissioner's seat on the Federal Trade Commission, The American Prospect . His nomination could be announced during a hearing of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee on Tuesday. Mufarrige ran a "buy here, pay here" used-car business in Texas called CNJ Auto Finance for three years in the late 2000s. Such businesses have been criticized for predatory tactics like imposing high interest rates on consumers who have poor credit, targeting consumers who publicly file for bankruptcy, and rapidly repossessing vehicles if consumers default on their loans. Mufarrige's firm was unsuccessfully sued twice, once for taking vehicles without proper payment and another time for failure to pay property taxes. TAP's full report is available . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations after pressure from authorities: The Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta its last editorial meeting on Monday and closed its Moscow newsroom. It announced in October that it was being forced to shut down after the government designated it a "foreign agent," and cut its access to the Russian banking system. Authorities arrested an editor at the paper, Oleg Roldugin, in April, and last month they searched the home of editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov and questioned him. UN rights chief Volker Turk called Russia's crackdown on the publication "yet another devastating blow for remaining independent media" in the country. Novaya Gazeta was co-founded by Mikhail Gorbachev and funded with money from his Nobel Peace Prize. The paper was one of the few outlets that openly criticized Russia's war in Ukraine. France raises minimum wage 1.6% in attempt to quell protests: France will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% on December 1, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday, expediting an increase that was scheduled for January 2027. The increase raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros ($27), from 1,477.93 euros ($1,656) to 1,502 euros ($1,683). Lecornu told reporters this was "the second-largest rise in 20 years" and "not merely symbolic." It falls short of trade unions' demands, however. The French Democratic Confederation of Labour wants a raise of at least 100 euros, and the General Confederation of Labour has demanded a raise of about 150 euros. CGT head Sophie Binet called Monday's raise "crumbs." Hungarian police arrest brother of Viktor Orb an: Hungarian police Viktor Orban's younger brother Aron on Monday, on suspicion of "people smuggling" and other offenses, according to a press report shared by Prime Minister Peter Magyar. Viktor Orban wrote on X that he was "the real target" of the arrest. A 2025 investigation by the news site Telex linked Aron Orban and others to an alleged scheme involving visas for foreign guest workers. Magyar, who won the premiership in a landslide election in April, promised to investigate his predecessor's alleged corruption and abuse of power. 2,500+ people flee Darfur for Chad: A harvest failure, insufficient rainfall, and the ongoing civil war have 2,510 people to flee Darfur for Chad, the Sudan Tribune reported. Adam Rijal, a spokesperson for the General Coordination of Displaced Persons and Refugees, said that living conditions in Darfur are rapidly deteriorating. He said that the region desperately needs a surge in all kinds of aid--food, water, and medicine. Gunmen kill guard and 10 relatives, abduct 13 in northwest Nigeria: Gunmen a local security volunteer and 10 of his relatives in an attack in Nigeria's northwestern Zamfara state over the weekend, torching his house and abducting a further 13 relatives, Reuters reported. A police official said that the security guard, a member of a government-backed vigilante group, had helped state security forces fend off gang incursions in the area, leading the "bandits" to consider him "an obstacle to their activities." Security forces have been deployed to secure the hostages' release. Armed gangs have long raided villages in northwestern Nigeria, killing residents, abducting people for ransom, and looting homes. South African police arrest nine foreign nationals suspected of trying to join Russia 's war on Ukraine: South African police nine young men, ages 20 to 26, at Johannesburg's OR Tambo Airport on Sunday night, accusing them of seeking to fight in Russia's war in Ukraine. The arrests follow an investigation involving Interpol and local agencies. South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act bars mercenary activity, recruitment, and training. The arrests come amid concern that Africans, Asians, and South Americans are being lured to Russia with civilian job offers and forced into combat in Ukraine. Paraguay expands probe of collapsed bank Ueno, agents raid bank office: Paraguayan** prosecutors the digital bank Ueno's brokerage arm on Monday. The raid is part of a widening probe into Ueno, a huge bank whose collapse led to the resignation of Santiago Peña from the presidency last week. Following the raid, prosecutors shared images of ripped-up documents, including fragments of what appeared to be due-diligence reports and emails. Separately, Paraguay's Congress approved President Pedro Alliana's nomination of economist Jorge Schreiner to replace former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Tuesday. It also named the former banking regulator Fernando Rivarola, who warned the public about Ueno in a July report, to the board of the central bank. Like the former president Peña, Carvallo has business ties to Ueno. Both men were recently charged with breach of trust and administration and are in pretrial detention. Exxon Mobil reaches preliminary, nonbinding deal with Venezuela: ExxonMobil on Monday that it drafted a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela. The agreement is nonbinding, which allows Exxon to hedge its bets. The company said that "any future investment would require stable policies, clear regulations, strong investment protections and competitive returns." The deal is a symbolic win for Trump and a reversal of Exxon Mobil's position in January, when CEO Darren Woods called Venezuela "uninvestable." Venezuela has twice seized Exxon's assets in the country. Taiwan accuses China of "area denial" drills in Western Pacific: On Tuesday, Taiwanese** Defense Minister Wellington Koo China of conducting "area denial" drills in the Western Pacific. Koo told reporters that China used its Liaoning carrier group and other naval formations in the process. "Anti-access area denial" is a military tactic designed to deter outside forces from intervening in conflict. Last week, Taiwan's security chief Joseph Wu said that more than 100 Chinese naval and Coast Guard ships were operating in the South China Sea and in the Pacific, and the defense ministry reported a large rise in Chinese aircraft in the area. He overcame immense opposition spending — and won decisively.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261110-1&t=1&akid=4241%2E587540%2EfbCFMb)
Peter,
Last week, Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim American elected to the U.S. Senate.
In the August Michigan primary, Abdul won by a single point, about 16,000 votes out of 1.5 million ballots cast. He was up against over $30 million of spending against him by AIPAC, and another $30 million in dark money and various corporate PACs backing his opponent. He was outspent 11-to-1, and he proved that message is more important than money.
This midterm election cycle was the most expensive in Michigan’s history. And Abdul overcame wave after wave of corporate spending while relying completely on grassroots funding for his campaign.
Races in Michigan, and around the country, sent a clear message to corporations trying to buy candidates: they can pour hundreds of millions of dollars in dark money into campaigns, but people power will come out on top.
Abdul won decisively. He proved that bold policy and moral leadership wins. In a deep purple swing state, Abdul proved that progressive policies and new ideas are popular and within reach.
He’s not only bringing a new progressive voice to the Senate, but he’ll help bring down the average age of sitting Senators. Abdul is over 20 years younger than the average age of the Senate, and when he takes office, he will be among the youngest sitting Senators.
This Michigan Senate race is why we do the work we do at Leaders We Deserve. The system is designed to favor older, whiter, richer establishment candidates. **But as more people reach voting age, a representation gap grows between the age and priorities of politicians and the age and priorities of the people.** We saw many wins last week, but in order to protect those wins, and keep this momentum going, we have to get to work now.

There's a line in _Hamilton_ where George Washington tells a young Alexander Hamilton, "Winning was easy, young man, governing's harder." It's a lesson Democrats would be wise to remember after Tuesday's historic election.
This was the [largest blue wave since Watergate](https://substack.com/redirect/efa3742f-fa2b-478c-acc0-c1e49f29e60d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But Democrats should be careful not to mistake a rejection of Donald Trump's policies for an unconditional embrace of their own party's ideas. Many Americans who voted blue weren't necessarily voting _for_ Democrats so much as they were voting _against_ the direction of the country, particularly rising costs driven by tariffs and the war in Iran.
Democrats often talk about being a big-tent party. But as we saw last Tuesday in competitive races across red and purple states like Georgia and Texas, winning means reaching beyond the Democratic base and persuading independents and moderates that Democrats can do a better job of governing. Even Pope Leo voted in the election - the first Pope ever to vote in a US election.
The fact that so many independent Americans have placed their trust in Democrats to do a better job should be humbling, not an invitation to take a victory lap.
Consider that Tuesday marked the seventh consecutive federal election in which control of at least one of Washington's three elected institutions--the House, Senate, or White House--changed hands. Americans keep voting for change, only to find themselves demanding it again two years later. If Democrats want to break that cycle, they need to show Americans that their trust wasn't misplaced through action and not just words.
Democrats shouldn't wait until January to start proving they can deliver. The lame-duck session going on now and the next two years offer an opportunity to lower costs and rebuild public trust through bipartisan cooperation. There are already encouraging signs. James Talarico, the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas, has expressed a willingness to work with President Trump on border security and immigration reform. It's the kind of sentiment that would have been difficult to imagine from a Democrat during Trump's first administration.

---|---|---
**Chart from[Bruce Mehlman's Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/ff22dc9a-9ab0-4eca-b062-4c8e4cc99609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Congress has several major pieces of legislation to address before the end of the year, giving Republicans and Democrats an opportunity to show Americans they can still work together. The most urgent is keeping the government open. Federal funding[ expires on December 11](https://substack.com/redirect/cd6f7929-a619-4951-b2f6-42822f1a8f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and after enduring[ the longest government shutdown in American history](https://substack.com/redirect/ccbcfd84-5d53-4baf-ab43-158082f80cf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last year--43 days--The last thing we need is a repeat.
Lawmakers must also pass the annual[ National Defense Authorization Act](https://substack.com/redirect/3642ae91-736b-4602-9ba3-757e524a25a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (NDAA), which sets our nation's defense priorities and supports the readiness of the men and women serving in uniform.
Then there's permitting reform, which sounds about as exciting as watching paint dry, but has enormous consequences for American families and businesses. It takes four years on average to approve and connect new energy projects to the electrical grid, even as demand for electricity continues to grow. (They should've called my friend and messaging guru, Frank Luntz up at West Point for some advice.) One [recent analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/e5fbd59e-3fc5-4b01-a9d1-a2f3da2622f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that power plants completed in 2025 had waited a median of 61 months to connect to the grid, compared with 22 months in 2008. Streamlining these processes could help bring more affordable energy online (including clean power), strengthen domestic manufacturing, and improve our economic competitiveness. It's failed the last five years, but Semafor reports: "We believe we have the votes to proceed," said Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I. He said he believes the bill is also in "very good shape" in the House...The legislation aims to speed up big electricity projects and force data centers to pay for their share of electric grid usage. Its passage would represent a significant feat, considering the failed permitting efforts of the past five years. "We don't have to wait for a new Congress to start lowering costs," said Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.
And here's another seemingly mundane issue with surprisingly high stakes: sulfur. Yes, sulfur. That smelly stuff you vaguely remember from chemistry class is actually a matter of national security. It's essential to producing fertilizer, processing critical minerals, and manufacturing materials our military depends on. And as the war in Iran has reminded us, something as basic as sulfur can become a serious problem when global supply chains are disrupted. They're essential to protecting America's security and prosperity.
And we cannot talk seriously about affordability without addressing healthcare. Americans are already struggling with rising insurance premiums, and the average benchmark Affordable Care Act marketplace [premium is increasing another 13% in 2027](https://substack.com/redirect/aa2a95ed-37fe-4d2a-8201-9f2c28a802c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's on top of a 26% increase the previous year. Families shouldn't have to choose between paying for healthcare and keeping up with their other bills.
These are real problems requiring real solutions. They also present an opportunity for Republicans and Democrats to work across party lines and find common ground.
**The New Congress**
When the new Congress convenes in January, Democrats should arrive with a clear 100-hour and 100-day agenda focused on affordability, ethics, and restoring trust in government.
I know the value of such a plan firsthand. Twenty years ago, I was part of the Democratic majority elected to Congress in another historic wave. Thirty one of us arrived in Washington with a 100-hour agenda that included ethics reform (no revolving door lobbying or gifts), implementing the recommendations of the 9/11 Commission, and raising the federal minimum wage to $7.25 (which hasn't been raised federally since then). We understood that winning an election was only the beginning. Voters expected us to deliver. Here's me talking to Will Cain about earning trust back with action:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdb865d-4a90-4c55-ad39-4539f1eb56e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Today's Democrats should approach their new majority with that same sense of urgency. That means pursuing meaningful congressional ethics reform, including restrictions on stock trading (must be in a blind trust) and not participating in prediction markets by members of Congress, while making affordability and the cost of living a central priority.
The Democratic victory was a mandate to address affordability and restore accountability, not a blank check for partisan retaliation. That doesn't mean ignoring wrongdoing or looking the other way when federal laws have been violated. Congress has a responsibility to conduct oversight, and no administration should be above the law. But investigations must be grounded in evidence and focused on legitimate misconduct, rather than becoming a substitute for governing.
Americans are tired of watching Washington investigate itself while their bills keep getting higher. They deserve a Congress capable of doing more than assigning blame.
* * *
## Shrinking Veteran Leadership in Congress
Here's a blurb from our friends at the Nimitz Report I found alarming: "Veterans are [expected to account for approximately 15% of the incoming Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/81f15f36-b57d-4893-bbe5-435052362014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), down from 19% in the current Congress and potentially the lowest share since at least the 1970s. According to Military Times, at least 57 veterans had secured seats as of November 5, with additional races still undecided...The incoming Congress will include both returning veteran lawmakers and newly elected members with military backgrounds."
## Veterans Day Engagements this Week & Next Month
First off, Happy 251st Birthday to our legendary US Marine Corps today - which was founded in Tun Tavern in Philadelphia, PA, on November 10, 1775. Tomorrow is Veterans Day, and as many of you know, we're passionate about providing access to capital for the next generation of 'vetrepreneurs' \- as a venture capitalist (over $300 million invested), lecturer at Wharton (Huntsman Hall named after a Navy Veteran), and entrepreneur myself. Leaders solve problems and when 50% of World War II veterans came home and started their own small business but it's now less than 5% of Post 9/11 veterans who do so, there's a lot of work we have to do.
Pretty excited to be heading back down to Walmart in Bentonville, Arkansas to share the stage with the Walmart CEO John Furner, who started as an hourly associate and now leads 2.1 million associates around the world - as well the UHP (Unlock Human Potential) founder Matt Heese, an Army Veteran who runs one of the country's largest skill trades academies. It's especially ironic to be there on Veterans Day as Walmart's founder Sam Walton was a WWII veteran who founded the world's largest retailer. Lastly, this Thursday night we'll be at the US Chamber of Commerce Hiring Our Heroes Gala as the presenter giving out the Capital One Small Business Award (can't tell you who's receiving it yet, I don't know until I open up the envelope).
I mention these events because it's about building trust with all of you - every day, every week, and every month - not just on holidays like tomorrow. If you can, join us next month as we have our 5th annual [Army Navy Policy Conference](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1c5d2d-466e-4a85-a9f3-a25b28006b2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Friday, December 11th at Fordham Business School (it's the day before the iconic Army Navy Game).
**And as a thank-you to our subscribers, you can attend free using the code PJM/G9.**
We're bringing together more than 200 leaders for an afternoon of conversation, collaboration, and networking. Our goal is to create a room where roughly one-third of attendees come from the senior military and veteran leadership community, one-third are cadets, junior officers, and emerging leaders, and one-third are executives, investors, and industry experts. It's an opportunity for the next generation to learn directly from those who have led in uniform, business, and public service--and for all of us to build relationships that can make a difference long after the conference ends.
We'll have an extraordinary lineup of leaders from the military, technology, finance, and national security communities, including Oracle CEO Mike Sicilia, alongside senior military and industry executives. The program will explore everything from defense technology and entrepreneurship to finance, media, and the opportunities available to veterans after service.
Hope you'll be part of the next generation of leaders who truly do what they can to earn your trust again...Go Army and Happy birthday Marines!

The DLCC is on the front lines, tracking more than **_100 races_** where recounts may be needed. These races include districts in battlegrounds like Minnesota, New Hampshire, and many others. Here’s how we help:
* **Help fund and support the legal costs** associated with recounts.
* **Work directly with teams on the ground** to provide guidance on how to navigate the process.
* **Coordinate with national partners** to understand which recounts have the highest stakes.
* **Focus our efforts where they matter most,** prioritizing races where recounts could make a real difference in the outcome of a race.

name: U.S. Senator Chris Murphy
subject: An update
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Chris Murphy
body:
As you may have heard, I was diagnosed with a small hemorrhagic stroke the Saturday before Election Day.
#

I wanted to reach out and thank you for the outpouring of support my family and I have received in recent days. As you may have heard, I was diagnosed with a small hemorrhagic stroke the Saturday before Election Day.
I realize though there is a good chance that news did not reach many of you — especially with the abundance of wins Democrats had last Tuesday.
But before I share more about my diagnosis, let’s talk about those incredible results.
Over the past two years, Donald Trump turned the White House into a 24/7 corruption machine. While Americans were paying more at the grocery store, and at the gas station, Trump was trading pardons for donations, selling our advanced technology in exchange for investments in the Trump family crypto ventures, manipulating the stock market and oil futures via Truth Social post, and raising costs across the board with his unpopular war with Iran.
For two years, not a single Republican in Congress dared to rein him in, and on Tuesday, voters delivered an emphatic message about where their priorities lay.
It is the beginning of the end of the Trump era. All across the country, we saw candidates win by standing up to the billionaires and corporations who rigged the system and broke our democracy.
Democrats must now hold this Administration and its corrupt allies accountable and also simultaneously fight for an aggressively populist agenda to unrig our economy and deliver for working people across the political spectrum.
Thank you for the work we’ve done together to make this opportunity happen. Your energy was the foundation upon which we began building a movement.
As we look ahead, Democrats have been given an enormous responsibility to use the power and trust placed in us by the American people to deliver change. Just going back to the way things were is simply not enough.
I cannot wait to get back to work with all of my new colleagues, my old friends, and the incredible trust that the American people have placed in our party to govern.
While you may not be hearing from me as much as I focus on my rehabilitation, just know that my doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far and expect that I will make a full recovery. I want to thank them, and all of the staff, nurses, and healthcare professionals that have taken care of me and my family.
Thank you, again, for all the support you have shown me, not just in the last week, but throughout the years as we’ve built this movement.
Every best wish,
Chris Murphy
