# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241173%2E444211%2EeiV8jq)
After more than 20 years, Democrats won the Texas State House.
Here’s how it came together.
**_For the first time since 1974, there was a Democrat running for every single seat on the ballot._** That didn’t happen by accident. Powered by People held organizing rallies, reached out personally to people we thought would make great candidates, and stood with them once they filed. Because of that work, every voter had a real choice.
Then we went out and found the voters. We spent years meeting them where they are: on college campuses, at concerts, and in coffeehouses. We registered them and talked with them one conversation at a time.
Look at the closest races:
* **Tarrant County:** Democrats won three House seats here that Republicans held, and our voters turned out in every one. Beth Llewellyn McLaughlin won HD-97 by 1,439 votes. 523 of our voters cast ballots in her district, equal to more than a third of her margin.

* **Brazos County (HD-14):** The count isn’t finished, and the Democrat is ahead by 315 votes. 1,438 of our voters cast ballots in this district, more than four times that lead. Nearly half of them, 666, registered or updated their registration with us this year, and 89% are between 18 and 29.

* **Harris County (HD-126):** Stefanie Bord is up by 265 votes for an open seat Republicans have held, and ballots are still being counted. 422 voters we contacted turned out, about 1.6 times her lead. Of everyone we contacted in the district, 78% voted.

Of the House seats Democrats won from Republicans, nine were in districts where we organized consistently. Six of those nine came down to fewer than 2,000 votes, and our voters numbered in the hundreds in every one.
**That’s what this kind of organizing does. When races are this close, every person we reach and register can decide the outcome.**
Our work didn’t stop on Election Day. Powered by People is already back on campuses registering students and showing them what’s at stake. We’re adding new voters to the rolls right now.
**We stay active all year because you can’t grow the number of Texas voters in the last few months before an election. Every person we register this year is a new voter in 2028, and that’s how we go into the next election even stronger.**

clean_body: After more than 20 years, Democrats won the Texas State House. Here’s how it came together. For the first time since 1974, there was a Democrat running for every single seat on the ballot. That didn’t happen by accident. Powered by People held organizing rallies, reached out personally to people we thought would make great candidates, and stood with them once they filed. Because of that work, every voter had a real choice. Then we went out and found the voters. We spent years meeting them where they are: on college campuses, at concerts, and in coffeehouses. We registered them and talked with them one conversation at a time. Look at the closest races: Tarrant County: Democrats won three House seats here that Republicans held, and our voters turned out in every one. Beth Llewellyn McLaughlin won HD-97 by 1,439 votes. 523 of our voters cast ballots in her district, equal to more than a third of her margin. Brazos County (HD-14): The count isn’t finished, and the Democrat is ahead by 315 votes. 1,438 of our voters cast ballots in this district, more than four times that lead. Nearly half of them, 666, registered or updated their registration with us this year, and 89% are between 18 and 29. Harris County (HD-126): Stefanie Bord is up by 265 votes for an open seat Republicans have held, and ballots are still being counted. 422 voters we contacted turned out, about 1.6 times her lead. Of everyone we contacted in the district, 78% voted. Of the House seats Democrats won from Republicans, nine were in districts where we organized consistently. Six of those nine came down to fewer than 2,000 votes, and our voters numbered in the hundreds in every one. That’s what this kind of organizing does. When races are this close, every person we reach and register can decide the outcome. Our work didn’t stop on Election Day. Powered by People is already back on campuses registering students and showing them what’s at stake. We’re adding new voters to the rolls right now. We stay active all year because you can’t grow the number of Texas voters in the last few months before an election. Every person we register this year is a new voter in 2028, and that’s how we go into the next election even stronger. Thank you, Powered by People

| | This Veterans Day, join Debbie Kraulidis for a special conversation with award-winning actor Jim Caviezel, best known for his roles in The Passion of the Christ and Sound of Freedom. Jim joins us to discuss his latest film, Ghost Soldier, a modern-day David and Goliath story about courage, conviction, and standing up for what is right. He shares what drew him to the story, how his faith influences the roles he chooses, and why Hollywood needs more stories that celebrate heroism, sacrifice, and the fight for freedom. As we honor the men and women who have served our nation, Jim reminds us why courage, faith, and a willingness to stand for what is right still matter. The man likely to be the next speaker of the House says the White House's new chief of staff gets no phone calls. Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's "This Week" there will be no "opportunity" to work with American hero Stephen Miller, after posting Friday that Miller's "presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor." So much for the healing. For what it's worth, Jeffries has his metaphors mixed up: Stephen Miller is the radiation, the chemo, the miracle antidote to the cancerous rot of the American Republic. Dylan Kresak of the Daily Caller News Foundation has the story. Calley Means, a former adviser to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., told Joe Rogan that a Susie Wiles aide put the February glyphosate executive order on his desk and told him it "was final." The order calls the weedkiller a farm-security asset, which is a tough sell to anyone who came to MAHA to get it off their food. The story also runs an X post from James Blair (@JamesBlairUSA), who writes "Again not true" and says he told Means he'd consider suing if Means defamed him. The Washington Post reports, citing former Trump campaign adviser Alex Bruesewitz and three unnamed sources, that Laura Loomer took undisclosed payments to post for clients trying to reach the president, $3,000 to $5,000 or more a post by two sources' telling. Bank records the Post reviewed show more than $60,000 in four payments since May 2025, though they don't say what for. Loomer denies charging $5,000 a tweet and says her business is opposition research. Videos from @TheMaineWire on X : Jon walks through what it would take after Pingree's Sunday post about "reforming the Supreme Court." Congress can change the number of justices by law, but it has to pass both chambers, get past the filibuster and get signed, and the president still picks the nominees. Then he asks what stops the other party from doing the same thing next time. About 4 minutes 40 seconds. : Joe Sokol on Monday's swearing-in of three new Bangor councilors who won on homelessness, public drug use and needles, and why the council handed the gavel to second-year member Daniel Carson instead. About 4 and a half minutes. Maine Wire TV If you're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and. You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's Monday's episode... : Tom Shattuck, Jon, Graham and I take on the CD2 count, where Shenna Bellows left the door open to a Dunlap win after Dunlap himself conceded and LePage headed to new-member orientation in Washington. We play Trump's 60 Minutes line that deportations "might be too tough" against his decision to make Stephen Miller chief of staff the same week. Then we get into Chellie Pingree's Supreme Court talk and how Maine handles overseas ballots. About 67 minutes. Today's Political Events 1\. CD2 ranked-choice tabulation, day 2 : LePage already won, but the count continues. 2\. Veterans Day : Wednesday, Nov. 11. Parades in Saco-Biddeford, Portland (10:30 a.m., Longfellow Square) and Bangor-Brewer (10:15 a.m., Vista Way, Brewer) (See: ). 3\. Maine GOP chair race : The chairman appoints a nominating committee Sunday, Nov. 15, ahead of an early-January vote. 4\. Legislature picks constitutional officers : Wednesday, Dec. 2, in joint session, including the next attorney general. We've been reporting for weeks now that the lead candidate is Anne Carney, a "climate lawyer," and former state lawmaker from Cape Elizabeth. One of the Soros blogs reports this week that Yarmouth lawyer Tim Shannon also thinks he's in the mix. 5\. Lewiston mayoral runoff : Tuesday, Dec. 15, Rick LaChapelle vs. Mayor Carl Sheline. Absentee requests are due Dec. 10 at 4 p.m. Around the Web (WGME) Video from outside ICE's Scarborough facility Monday shows protesters with an "Abolish ICE" sign, at least one long gun and a guy in fatigues with "NOT A COP" on the back. According to Rep. Chellie Pingree, ICE says the armed protesters are why it sent more agents. Pingree's complaint is about the agents. WGME has the story. * That's Tuesday. name: Wes Moore
subject: Marching orders
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2292%2E1086043%2Et_gtLW)
Peter, I wanted to take a minute to thank you.
Four years ago, you took a chance on somebody who had never held elected office before. You believed we could do things that others said couldn’t be done.
You believed that we could confront the violent crime that devastated our communities. You believed that we could turn around failing scores in our public schools. And you believed that we could restart our economy that had stalled.
Together, we did -- and I am proud of the progress we’ve made. But last week’s election results are not a pat on the back. They’re our marching orders.
**That’s why this legislative session we will continue the greatest public safety turnaround story in America by investing in both local law-enforcement and in our people.**
We will build the best public education system in America because every child in Maryland deserves a school that believes in them.
We will grow and diversify our economy so we are less dependent on Washington. That means more jobs, higher wages and more Marylanders building wealth.
We will keep working to make life more affordable for Marylanders -- investing in childcare and affordable housing and fighting to bring down energy bills.
**I know our goals are ambitious and audacious. But that’s exactly what you voted for.**
I’m so humbled to be your Governor and for your vote of confidence.
Now, let’s get to work.
-- Wes Moore

Before you go... Building a Maryland where we Leave No One Behind will take all of us, and Wes Moore needs our help to keep this movement going strong. **[Will you chip in any amount-- even just $5 -- to support Wes’ mission today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261110-1.mZYCD7&refcode=em-20261110-1&t=2&akid=2292%2E1086043%2Et_gtLW)** **[Donate »](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261110-1.mZYCD7&refcode=em-20261110-1&t=3&akid=2292%2E1086043%2Et_gtLW)**

Whether you signed up to learn more, applied but were not assigned, or spent a long day helping voters at your polling place, you were part of the effort that kept our elections running smoothly, fairly, and safely. Whether you served on Election Day or are thinking about getting involved next time, your experience helps us figure out what worked, what didn’t, and how we can better support poll workers in future elections. Yesterday,
in an unsigned order, the Supreme Court cleared the way for Trump’s border
wall to tear through Big Bend National Park in Texas.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20261110.dYQ3zy&refcode=em20261110-61987&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61987%2E1407376%2EfZaGd8 ]CNN Headline: Supreme Court allows Trump to continue border wall
construction in Big Bend Region of Texas.

A federal judge had halted the project. The question is simple: Did
Trump’s administration have the power to ignore environmental laws? That
question hasn’t been answered. The Supreme Court let construction resume
anyway.

Trump’s plan for the region is to build more than 300 miles of walls and
roads. To push it through, his Department of Homeland Security waived the
protections that normally apply to a project like this.

Environmental laws, gone. Historic preservation, gone. Protections for
Native American artifacts, gone.

This is how the Court's majority operates now. Trump asks, and the
far-right majority delivers through rushed, unsigned orders. No full
argument. No name on the decision. No justice held accountable.

Why now? Because Republicans just lost the House and the Senate. So Trump
is running to the one branch voters can’t touch: a Supreme Court stacked
with ultra-conservative justices, three of them handpicked by Trump
himself.

And this isn’t the first time. The justices have already greenlit Trump’s
mass deportation plan again and again, and immigrant families are paying
the price.

It’s corruption, plain and simple, and the people deserve to know it.

That’s where Demand Justice PAC comes in. We expose every ruling this
Court tries to slip past the public. We hold the justices accountable. And
we make sure voters know exactly who is rubber-stamping Trump’s
authoritarianism.

But we can’t do it without grassroots supporters like you.

| | | Fellow Conservative, last Tuesday did not go our way. I'm not going to spin it. Democrats now control the Senate and the House. And Texas just sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate for the first time in nearly 40 years. What happens in Texas happens to all of us. But I'm not writing today to sound another alarm. A lot of good people worked their hearts out this cycle. You were one of them. So before the pundits and consultants in Washington write the official story of what happened, **_I want to hear it from you._** **That 's why I put together a short [2026 Exit Poll.](https://trk.email.tedcruz._wccCShj6i4aQ)** It takes one minute. __What did we get wrong? What issues should I fight hardest on now? How can I best serve you over the next two years?__ There are no wrong answers. Be blunt. I can take it. [[**BEGIN 2026 MIDTERM SURVEY ->]**](https://trk.email.tedcruz._g2GGbUlfA) Losing the majority doesn't end this fight. It changes the job. With the radical left setting the agenda in Washington, my job is to stand in the way and block their socialist wish list. I want your priorities leading the charge when I do. Thank you for standing with me. I appreciate you more than you know, Ted Cruz

name: Chris Deluzio
subject: “Trickle-down economics” is a scam.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
And it must be crushed
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=166%2E42639%2EyuXMJW)
With last week's wins across our Commonwealth and across our country, Democrats have the chance to break corrupt corporate power, get their money out of our politics, and crush the scam that is "trickle-down economics."
But, unfortunately, this is that time when many of the politicians who take that corporate money stop talking ... and yes, that includes some Democrats.
They don't want to name the villains in this story.
But the American Dream did not just disappear.
Whether we call them robber barons or oligarchs, the corrupt and powerful have been ripping away the American Dream for decades.
They've consolidated huge monopolies.
They've hoarded enormous wealth for themselves.
They've cheered on lousy trade deals.
At the same time: Workers’ paychecks fell. Small businesses get crushed. Jobs shipped overseas. And the costs go up for all of us.
Then, those *villains* pour billions and billions of dollars into elections to protect an economy rigged for their benefit ... propped up by a corrupt system of campaign finance.
The result is what we've all seen. The robber barons, the oligarchs ... they get bought and paid for politicians to give them tax giveaways and saddle all of us with generationally crippling debt.
They call it trickle-down economics, but we know what it is.
It's a scam.
And if we have the courage -- and we must -- it can end on our watch, and we can create a government and an economy that works for all of us and not just the oligarchs and robber barons of this country.
Let's get it done.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

## **The 411 on the Lame-Duck Session**
Congress is back in Washington, and the clock is officially ticking. The lame-duck session is upon us, and there is zero time to waste.
Between now and January 3, 2027, when the new Congress is sworn in, Senate leadership and the White House must get crystal clear on their top priorities. The simple math of Capitol Hill dictates that once the clock runs out, any unconfirmed nominee or unfinished piece of conservative legislation dies.
[| | | | | Fox News Politics

LAME DUCK: Congress returns to Capitol Hill this week staring down a Dec. 11 government shutdown deadline, leadership elections, and a stack of unfinished legislation before Democrats take the reins in January. Republicans have to navigate a farm bill, transportation ...

There are two non-negotiables that must be executed over these final weeks:
* **Clear the Judicial & Executive Nominees: **Priority appointments - ambassadors, deputy secretaries, key agency directors, and federal judges - must be fast-tracked immediately. President Trump says there are 161 unconfirmed positions -- prioritize them.
* **Pass Essential & Conservative Legislation: **Beyond must-pass items like government funding and the National Defense Authorization act (NDAA), key legislative wins like the SAVE America Act and codifying border security policies must be pushed over the finish line.

The Senate cannot operate on a casual schedule of two-day workweeks and mid-session retreats. Lawmakers need to be working 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through January 3. As legendary coach Bill Belichick famously put it: _Do your job._
I get thats more work that most senators are used to but you ran for this office -- take Thanksgiving and Christmas off -- but that's it.
Today's issue breaks down why this lame-duck window is our last bite at the apple, how Chuck Schumer plans to stall every nominee, and the exact steps leadership must take right now.

In any sane world, the Republican Party would be falling over itself to impeach Pete Hegseth, if for no other reason than the political points they could score with the American people after last week's historic midterm loss for the GOP.
Hegseth is an unpopular buffoon, plain and simple. In a sea of incompetent boobs, he is by far the one who has caused the most damage, embarrassed this nation the most, and hurt us the most on the international stage, behind, of course, his boss, Donald Trump. The vast majority of Americans hate him. He's destroying the Pentagon. He's weakening the military. He's losing this war. He's destroying the economy and the global energy market. He's a performative poser. And he's made all of us in this country dramatically less safe.
This should be an easy call, now that Thomas Massie has moved forward a discharge petition to impeach Hegseth. But the Republican Party is nothing but a bunch of fucking cowards.
I expect we'll have a few Republican members who will vote to impeach Hegseth in the House, and maybe a few, like Senator Thom Tillis as he enters retirement, who will vote to remove him in the Senate. But ultimately, the vast majority of these hacks are going to fall in line, support their king, and do what they're told. And that's the whole problem.
They should remove him because he continues to purge highly qualified, experienced personnel inside the United States military who actually know what the fuck they're doing. Because someday we might need them to defend us.
They should remove him because he's denying benefits to the families of those who have lost their lives in this illegal war that he and Donald Trump started out of choice and stupidity, rather than patriotism or a sense of keeping us safe.
* * *

* * *
They should remove him for ordering a double-tap Tomahawk missile strike on an elementary school in Iran that killed 120 children and 36 civilians, most of them parents and teachers. The deadliest U.S. strike on civilians in the 21st century. For reportedly ordering his military to "kill everyone" in a follow-up strike on boats in the Caribbean, in violation of the Geneva Conventions and the Pentagon's own laws of war.
They should remove him for demanding the military livestream the firing-squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood. A demand so despicable, so outrageous, that even Donald Trump had to backtrack his own support for holding the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century.
They should remove him, if for no other reason than the fact that he and Donald Trump keep lying about the number of people who have been killed or wounded in this war.
And this comes back to a broader point I've been writing about since Tuesday's election. These people have learned absolutely nothing. And they will continue to learn absolutely nothing. They're not capable of introspection. Pete Hegseth, genuinely, to his core, believes he is doing a great job. He believes he should be the next president. That's why he's apparently making moves to step aside eventually and go run, even though he's proven himself to be wholly incompetent, dangerous, reckless, and unqualified.
Trump thinks he's doing a great job too. He was on 60 Minutes the other night talking about how we're still living in the golden age of America. He was at a press conference yesterday talking about how Pete Hegseth has won this war in Iran, something nobody believes.
It's a damn shame what's become of the Republican Party.
You would think that after a historic election where Democrats picked up what I think will ultimately be 56 Senate seats and an unbelievable number of House seats, after flipping entire states, like Texas, Republicans would finally have an incentive to look inward.
Losing Texas which should send a cold chill down the spine of every Republican operative and politician in this country, should be an opportunity that they might take to learn something. It's the kind of political reckoning that should force a party to ask itself some difficult questions about where it went wrong, why voters abandoned it, and what it needs to do differently. But no chance. They can't change. They're not capable of change..Apparently, even that isn't enough.
Rather than take a shred of responsibility for their own failures, they'd rather keep blaming everyone else. Trans kids. Hardworking immigrants. Anyone and everyone except the people actually running the Grand Old Party into the ground.
* * *

_My team and I use it because context matters._

* * *
And that's what makes this whole thing so remarkable. Republicans didn't just lose an election. They were handed an unmistakable message by the American people, and they seem utterly incapable of learning a damn thing from it.
I firmly believe this Republican Party needs to be burned to the ground and the earth salted. And at this point, I don't even care if something arises out of it. I want good human beings in office who are going to wake up every day and try to do what's right, who are going try to improve people's lives, make sure we're safe, and be fucking normal. That's why I'm so excited about last Tuesday. We elected a bunch of normal people who just want to get shit done, like Annie Andrews and James Talarico. And if Republicans won't learn the lesson they should have learned last week, then we're going to do this all again in 2028, and Democrats have to cast the widest possible net when we do.
We need to be tough. Sometimes we're going to be mean. That's what it takes to win. But we can't ever lose sight of the fact that we're trying to help improve people's lives. This is a nation of people who are struggling right now, working hard, doing everything right, fighting to build lives of dignity for themselves and for their families. And we can deliver for them. We should start by doing everything we can to limit the damage that Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth and the rest of this administration are doing.
And I want to come back to that press conference yesterday. Because Trump also repeatedly said that we haven't lost a single life in this war.
That's disgusting. At least 21 families will never be made whole again because of the loss of life. You can feel however you want about this conflict, but those are brave souls who stepped forward to serve this nation and keep Americans safe. And their memory is being disrespected by the commander in chief and his rabid lapdog, Pete Hegseth.
That's who Republicans are protecting if they keep him in that job.
I'm going to keep writing about this every step of the way, and I'm going to call out every Republican who chooses Hegseth over those families. If that matters to you, become a paid subscriber. Your support is what lets me do this work independently, without anyone telling me what I can and can't say.
Show them we can fight. Show them we can win. And I believe the American people will reward us in the end.
With urgency,
--Mike

They're not capable of introspection. Pete Hegseth, genuinely, to his core, believes he is doing a great job. He believes he should be the next president. That's why he's apparently making moves to step aside eventually and go run, even though he's proven himself to be wholly incompetent, dangerous, reckless, and unqualified. Trump thinks he's doing a great job too. He was on 60 Minutes the other night talking about how we're still living in the golden age of America. He was at a press conference yesterday talking about how Pete Hegseth has won this war in Iran, something nobody believes. It's a damn shame what's become of the Republican Party. You would think that after a historic election where Democrats picked up what I think will ultimately be 56 Senate seats and an unbelievable number of House seats, after flipping entire states, like Texas, Republicans would finally have an incentive to look inward. Losing Texas which should send a cold chill down the spine of every Republican operative and politician in this country, should be an opportunity that they might take to learn something. It's the kind of political reckoning that should force a party to ask itself some difficult questions about where it went wrong, why voters abandoned it, and what it needs to do differently. But no chance. They can't change. They're not capable of change..Apparently, even that isn't enough. Rather than take a shred of responsibility for their own failures, they'd rather keep blaming everyone else. Trans kids. Hardworking immigrants. Anyone and everyone except the people actually running the Grand Old Party into the ground. When a story feels too tidy, I always ask: what 's missing? Ground News shows how the same story is covered across the political spectrum and highlights blind spots most outlets ignore. My team and I use it because context matters. Try it today! And that's what makes this whole thing so remarkable. Republicans didn't just lose an election. They were handed an unmistakable message by the American people, and they seem utterly incapable of learning a damn thing from it. I firmly believe this Republican Party needs to be burned to the ground and the earth salted. And at this point, I don't even care if something arises out of it. I want good human beings in office who are going to wake up every day and try to do what's right, who are going try to improve people's lives, make sure we're safe, and be fucking normal. That's why I'm so excited about last Tuesday. We elected a bunch of normal people who just want to get shit done, like Annie Andrews and James Talarico. And if Republicans won't learn the lesson they should have learned last week, then we're going to do this all again in 2028, and Democrats have to cast the widest possible net when we do. We need to be tough. Sometimes we're going to be mean. That's what it takes to win. But we can't ever lose sight of the fact that we're trying to help improve people's lives. This is a nation of people who are struggling right now, working hard, doing everything right, fighting to build lives of dignity for themselves and for their families. And we can deliver for them. We should start by doing everything we can to limit the damage that Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth and the rest of this administration are doing. And I want to come back to that press conference yesterday. Because Trump also repeatedly said that we haven't lost a single life in this war. That's disgusting. At least 21 families will never be made whole again because of the loss of life. You can feel however you want about this conflict, but those are brave souls who stepped forward to serve this nation and keep Americans safe. And their memory is being disrespected by the commander in chief and his rabid lapdog, Pete Hegseth. That's who Republicans are protecting if they keep him in that job. I'm going to keep writing about this every step of the way, and I'm going to call out every Republican who chooses Hegseth over those families. If that matters to you, become a paid subscriber. Your support is what lets me do this work independently, without anyone telling me what I can and can't say. Show them we can fight. Show them we can win. And I believe the American people will reward us in the end. With urgency, --Mike P.S. A relentless barrage of phone calls continues to flood both the House and Senate, with voters from around the country urging Democrats not to make **Hakeem Jeffries** the speaker of the House nor **Chuck Schumer** majority leader in the Senate. The contest in the Senate came alive on Monday when advisers to Sen. **Chris Van Hollen** said he was openly considering a challenge to Schumer.
[In a new video, Van Hollen](https://substack.com/redirect/34b2b1f6-5b1d-42c7-adc6-0f68369c8d00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is demanding Congress refuse to approve "one more penny" for the war in Iran and dared President **Donald Trump** to shut the government down to continue a conflict he promised he wouldn't start.

## Progressives Lay the Groundwork to Force a Vote on Ending Some Arms Sales to Israel
#### _Rep. Delia Ramirez told Drop Site she is in discussions with Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on bringing the Block The Bombs Act to the floor._
_Story by Tom Perkins_
Progressives in Congress are already pressuring House leadership for a vote next session on the Block The Bombs Act, which would end U.S. sales for at least some weapons to Israel. The organizing comes as history's most pro-Palestinian Congress will sit in 2027, and the Congressional Progressive Caucus (CPC) will expand its power as its membership grows to unprecedented numbers.
Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), who authored the current session's Block The Bombs legislation, told Drop Site News she has already had initial discussions with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries about bringing the bill to the floor, and more conversations are planned for the coming days.
Ramirez said she "did not get a direct 'no'" and she is optimistic because of progressives' new power in Congress, Israel's dismal polling among Democrats, and because voters sent a message by electing at least 16 new pro-peace candidates in November, some of whom defeated among Israel's staunchest congressional allies.
"Our caucus is going to ask the question are you pro-peace or pro-genocide?'" Ramirez said. "The American people have made clear what side they are on, and what they expect of their leaders."
The current Block The Bombs bill, which has 82 cosponsors, was introduced in September 2025 and would stop the president "from selling, transferring, or exporting certain defense articles or services to Israel, except in specified circumstances." The sales would be allowed only if Congress passes legislation specifying how the weapons would be used and Israel agrees to the terms. The precise scope of next session's legislation is unclear.
In January 2026, Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [told The Economist](https://substack.com/redirect/44c6d9d9-b814-4c59-9600-b13e02d6e2a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Israel was enacting a 10-year-plan to wean itself off U.S. weapons, and reiterated that point multiple times this year. In the days ahead of the election, President Donald Trump said the U.S. would no longer provide Israel with around $4 billion annually in support for weapons. On Monday, the liberal Zionist organization [J Street called for ending taxpayer support for sales](http://The liberal Zionist organization J Street has also called for ending taxpayer support for sales, though stopped short of a full embargo) and evaluating arms sales on a case-by-case basis, though it stopped short of calling for a full embargo.
"They've become a very successful country," Trump [said on November 3](https://substack.com/redirect/0091d20f-9a9a-4ff3-90f0-4c888e6d4004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "They don't need it, and we won't be paying any more." When asked why, he added, "Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?"
Meanwhile, calls for an arms embargo that would end all weapons sales to Israel has gained traction in the political mainstream. Among those supporting ending taxpayer assistance and barring weapons sales are Rep. [Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez](https://substack.com/redirect/f5977666-3475-4938-9660-0f4b3484e30a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (D-N.Y.), Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), and Senator-elect [Abdul El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/d72323b5-9df6-4bdf-8769-d1a3990e5ade?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (D-Mich.)--as well as incoming Reps. [Matt Little](https://substack.com/redirect/a88e64c4-4fa1-413c-8618-a9afde62ddc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (D-Minn.), [Chris Rabb](https://substack.com/redirect/ecf4125f-c0d0-40ea-a49f-b69ac9a05f4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (D-Pa.), and [Melat Kiros](https://substack.com/redirect/5221ab7a-d4ff-40fa-9fc6-b01662a11b5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (D-Colo.).
In July this year, over 100 Democrats voted to support Republican Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie's [amendment](https://substack.com/redirect/6ea66d99-5db0-4d9f-bc6a-4b9c9629aa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a State Department funding bill that would have eliminated approximately $3.3 billion in annual U.S. military assistance to Israel. The amendment still failed by a wide margin and Massie lost his primary after Trump backed his challenger and outside groups, including AIPAC's United Democracy Project, came in with [$37 million](https://substack.com/redirect/d1bc3f7a-9797-4b18-af33-55b5a11d6306?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in spending.
Jeffries opposed the Massie amendment and said in a letter to Democrats at the time that it was "overly broad in that it prohibits or would limit the use of funds for longstanding initiatives related to humanitarian aid, refugee resettlement, peace-building and U.S. Embassy operations."
However, Jeffries also called for a "major reset" between the U.S. and Israel.
When asked about the scope of next session's Block The Bombs bill, a spokesperson for Ramirez said the congress member did not have a comment.
A Jeffries spokesperson did not return a request for comment.
Ramirez added that she last week met with many of the pro-peace members-elect who ran on ending U.S. support for Israel's genocide and is strategizing about how to get the legislation to the floor. The CPC will play a key role in the effort.
The largest CPC ever will sit next session when it takes in 25 new members, though its total number will increase only slightly because some members are leaving. However, this new group will be more to the left than the preceding, and Ramirez said the caucus will be in its "strongest position ever" and is "expanding its authority and power." Not every current CPC member cosigned on Block The Bombs, and its leftward shift will likely increase the level of support.
The CPC is essential to getting Block The Bombs to the floor, Ramirez said, and she and the CPC chair, Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas), have had conversations about it. "We are being very strategic about organizing and adding more cosponsors," Ramirez added.
She also noted that progressives unseated staunch pro-Israel advocates like Reps. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) and Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), which gives the left more leverage. Not only did these wins send a message to leadership, it makes it safer for legislators who were previously on the fence to support the new legislation.
"When you think about moving legislation you've got to ask yourself 'What are your numbers? Where are your votes?'" Ramirez said. "And I know how to count and the truth is we're about to have the largest CPC ever."

Democrats would need roughly 40 members to vote for someone other than Jeffries to ensure he doesn't meet the threshold of 218--a much taller order than the handful of "no" votes that locked out Republican former Speaker Kevin McCarthy. such an approach was being considered. "I think that should be absolutely part of the conversation. But you have to remember, during that time, there was a very small margin that allowed for that kind of thing to happen," she said. "If it is an unopposed race, then there's really no material scenario until there is a race," she said. "My assessment would be that would be unrealistic. In a contested race [it's] a different situation." | ---|--- 4,214 likes Drop Site on Instagram: "Drop Site's Julian Andreone pressed Re... The situation presents something of a catch-22: Jeffries isn't vulnerable unless a challenger emerges, and a challenger won't emerge as long as Jeffries is seen as invulnerable. Democrats who organize against Jeffries, even privately, risk having their "lives made a living hell" if they try and fail. Many Democrats say privately they believe Jeffries will be much easier to move on major issues than was former Speaker Nancy Pelosi. Rep. Delia Ramirez , the lead sponsor of the Block The Bombs Act, which bars the transfer of some weapons to Israel, told Drop Site she met recently with Jeffries, and came away with the impression that Jeffries would be willing to put the bill on the floor. For more on that conversation and the looming fight over Block The Bombs, read Tom Perkins's dispatch below. As the new Congress convenes, Drop Site will be expanding its congressional coverage. To that end, we launched a fundraising campaign with a goal of raising $100,000 last week. We're more than 80% of the way to that goal.: | | ---|---|--- House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., conducts a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on November 9, 2026. Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images. Progressives Lay the Groundwork to Force a Vote on Ending Some Arms Sales to Israel Rep. Delia Ramirez told Drop Site she is in discussions with Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on bringing the Block The Bombs Act to the floor. Story by Tom Perkins Progressives in Congress are already pressuring House leadership for a vote next session on the Block The Bombs Act, which would end U.S. sales for at least some weapons to Israel. The organizing comes as history's most pro-Palestinian Congress will sit in 2027, and the Congressional Progressive Caucus (CPC) will expand its power as its membership grows to unprecedented numbers. Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), who authored the current session's Block The Bombs legislation, told Drop Site News she has already had initial discussions with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries about bringing the bill to the floor, and more conversations are planned for the coming days. Ramirez said she "did not get a direct 'no'" and she is optimistic because of progressives' new power in Congress, Israel's dismal polling among Democrats, and because voters sent a message by electing at least 16 new pro-peace candidates in November, some of whom defeated among Israel's staunchest congressional allies. "Our caucus is going to ask the question are you pro-peace or pro-genocide?'" Ramirez said. "The American people have made clear what side they are on, and what they expect of their leaders." The current Block The Bombs bill, which has 82 cosponsors, was introduced in September 2025 and would stop the president "from selling, transferring, or exporting certain defense articles or services to Israel, except in specified circumstances." The sales would be allowed only if Congress passes legislation specifying how the weapons would be used and Israel agrees to the terms. The precise scope of next session's legislation is unclear. In January 2026, Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Israel was enacting a 10-year-plan to wean itself off U.S. weapons, and reiterated that point multiple times this year. In the days ahead of the election, President Donald Trump said the U.S. would no longer provide Israel with around $4 billion annually in support for weapons. On Monday, the liberal Zionist organization liberal Zionist organization J Street has also called for ending taxpayer support for sales, though stopped short of a full embargo and evaluating arms sales on a case-by-case basis, though it stopped short of calling for a full embargo. "They've become a very successful country," Trump . "They don't need it, and we won't be paying any more." When asked why, he added, "Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?" Meanwhile, calls for an arms embargo that would end all weapons sales to Israel has gained traction in the political mainstream. Among those supporting ending taxpayer assistance and barring weapons sales are Rep. (D-N.Y.), Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), and Senator-elect (D-Mich.)--as well as incoming Reps. (D-Minn.), (D-Pa.), and (D-Colo.). In July this year, over 100 Democrats voted to support Republican Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie's to a State Department funding bill that would have eliminated approximately $3.3 billion in annual U.S. military assistance to Israel. The amendment still failed by a wide margin and Massie lost his primary after Trump backed his challenger and outside groups, including AIPAC's United Democracy Project, came in with in spending. Jeffries opposed the Massie amendment and said in a letter to Democrats at the time that it was "overly broad in that it prohibits or would limit the use of funds for longstanding initiatives related to humanitarian aid, refugee resettlement, peace-building and U.S. Embassy operations." However, Jeffries also called for a "major reset" between the U.S. and Israel. When asked about the scope of next session's Block The Bombs bill, a spokesperson for Ramirez said the congress member did not have a comment. A Jeffries spokesperson did not return a request for comment. Ramirez added that she last week met with many of the pro-peace members-elect who ran on ending U.S. support for Israel's genocide and is strategizing about how to get the legislation to the floor. The CPC will play a key role in the effort. The largest CPC ever will sit next session when it takes in 25 new members, though its total number will increase only slightly because some members are leaving. However, this new group will be more to the left than the preceding, and Ramirez said the caucus will be in its "strongest position ever" and is "expanding its authority and power." Not every current CPC member cosigned on Block The Bombs, and its leftward shift will likely increase the level of support. The CPC is essential to getting Block The Bombs to the floor, Ramirez said, and she and the CPC chair, Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas), have had conversations about it. "We are being very strategic about organizing and adding more cosponsors," Ramirez added. She also noted that progressives unseated staunch pro-Israel advocates like Reps. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) and Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), which gives the left more leverage. Not only did these wins send a message to leadership, it makes it safer for legislators who were previously on the fence to support the new legislation. "When you think about moving legislation you've got to ask yourself 'What are your numbers? Where are your votes?'" Ramirez said. "Are you going to run again?"
It's the question I've heard about 100 times in the past week, and the honest answer is, "I don't know." I won't lie. These last 15 months have been hard. They've been hard on me and on Barb. Committing to doing that again is a lot. We'll make that decision later.
The day after the election, many people assumed I'd run again. They took a single phrase from one of my Facebook posts as proof. I really appreciate that level of faith and confidence, but they were grasping at straws. I understood. I was the first in a long time to walk into some of these counties and say, "I'm a Democrat and here's why you should vote for me." They don't want me to walk away from that.
And I admit, some parts of the campaign were a lot of fun. I really enjoyed when people came up to me and told me how much they appreciated my standing up in rural Alabama and saying what they had always wanted to say. I enjoyed hearing that I gave them hope. To be honest, I even enjoyed having conversations with people who insisted I was a communist who wanted to open the border, abolish all the prisons and the police, and enact Sharia law. I seriously believe I may have been the first Democrat some of them had even spoken to face-to-face, and it was a lot of fun.
But it took over a year of my life and was exhausting.
That said, I haven't given up on these eleven counties in this great state.
I know Alabama deserves better representation than we have, and that's what we will work toward, but we need to understand the election we just went through, and we need a plan.
We're going to do what we did during the campaign: talk to people and develop that plan. We need to understand what went wrong this year and chart a better course for 2028. Does that mean my name will be on the ballot? I don't know, but in the meantime, stay tuned.
This fight ain't over, and it's going to be fun because we're fighting for a better Alabama.
We'll talk soon.

_**The Alabama Reflector:**_**" Democratic turnout soars across Alabama in midterm election"**
Across the state, voter turnout was slightly higher than in 2024, with participation surging five points from 38.9% to 43.9%. Votes for Democratic candidates surged in all 67 counties. Notably, while Gubernatorial Candidate Doug Jones was well known, most of the other Democrats running were relatively unknown and, in many cases, running for office for the first time. That level of public support indicates a significant desire for change across the state.

**AL.com: "**_**How did Shomari Figures win after redistricting? Alabama 's Black voters were 'mad as hell'"**_
In Alabama's newly redrawn 2nd Congressional District, Congressman Shomari Figures proved that Republican last-minute redistricting was as dumb as it seemed. Nationwide, mid-decade redistricting cost the GOP several House seats. The Alabama GOP's attempt to redistrict after the primaries backfired even more.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Voters made it clear in this year’s midterm elections: they want Democrats
in Congress to put forth a bold agenda and actually fight for it. That’s
exactly what our newly elected congressmembers are calling for.

Right now, everyone is talking about the future of Democratic leadership.

Our slate of new House members has made it clear: they have not yet even
seen an agenda bold enough to earn their vote for Hakeem Jeffries as
Speaker of the House.

Here’s what some of them had to say on the matter:

“As of right now, my vote is no. I know for sure that over 100,000
Angelenos voted for courage, they voted for change, and I think that what
I don’t know is what Representative Hakeem Jeffries is offering my
community and constituents of California’s 34th district for their vote...
Respectfully, [he] will have to work for our vote.”
— Angela Gonzales-Torres, CA-34

“I don’t think it’s about the individual. It’s about the agenda that
actually reflects the priorities of the American people... We all agree that
we have to reduce costs for working families, we all agree that we have to
root out corruption in government, we all agree that our foreign policy
has to actually reflect our values... and in order for us to be able to do
that, we need an agenda that’s bold enough to meet that vision.”
— Melat Kiros, CO-01

“I ran on Medicare for All. I ran to increase the minimum wage to a living
wage. I ran to end endless wars. So I want to know, man to man, where
[Rep. Hakeem Jeffries] stands on those issues. Because I haven’t had a
conversation with him... We’d like to see an agenda that is reflective of
the type of things that we ran on and won on.”
— Chris Rabb, PA-03

“What we’re saying is we’re undecided. We’re not going to rubber stamp
anything. We want to sit and have a conversation about the issues and what
the plan is going forward, and I think that’s what the American people
elected us to do.”
— Dr. Adam Hamawy, NJ-12

They’re right. As Melat said, “populist politics won the midterms,” and
our bold new leaders aren’t going to just rubber-stamp or coronate a
speaker without knowing what their plan is to lower costs, address the
data center crisis, get big money out of politics, and so much more.

Here's [a post-election breakdown from the Idaho Freedom Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/1b7e4b35-1bd6-4b13-925b-b9cf4b0330cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which a lot of people in the state follow. Go read it first, then come back to this article.
Okay, you read it? Good.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/addde880-14de-4c31-a634-89ca6e14e9fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
First off, look at where their "conservative losses" came from.
By their own admission, it was last May's primary. But Democrats didn't vote in the 2026 Idaho Republican primary. Republicans did. So lumping the loss of IFF's loyalists (who use the Freedom Index as their voting guide) into a blue-wave story is disingenuous at best because there was no blue wave in the 2026 Republican primary. It's nonsensical.
Now, IFF gets a lot right, especially on spending and fiscal issues. I scored 78% on their index this year. But look at what they call a "conservative": anyone who scores well on their "Freedom Index."
That's how they pick winners and losers.
This is the same index that rated a bill making it a crime to hire illegals a big fat ZERO (HB 700, 2026). It gave the same zero rating to a bill making AI child porn a felony (HB 465, 2024), basically hinting that it was a victimless crime. This is the same index that rated a bill saying the state can't steal from orphans as negative this year (HB 558, 2026), and the same index that rated a bill to get junk food out of EBT as bad too (HB 109, 2025).
I could go on but you get the point.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86d90e13-ab27-45b2-ad4b-b36f53dae43d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
To be fair, IFF isn't the only one doing this type of thing. It seems like everybody in this state has a scorecard of sorts, and everybody has an agenda. IACI (basically the Chamber of Commerce at the state level) only scores like 12 bills a year based on what its corporate members want, and I'm near the bottom of their favs list. Their PAC even backs leadership who fail their own scorecard, then goes after conservatives who score well. Makes no sense.
Farm Bureau has one too. They say they want a secure border, but when the bills to crack down on hiring illegals died this year, they didn't shed a tear (their lobbyist said E-Verify is the feds' job). Idaho Business for Education has one too. Back in 2021, 18 of the 19 Democrats in the Legislature scored a perfect 100 on it.
Point is that scorecards are a dime a dozen. You just have to do some digging to find out what each one is really pushing before you let it tell you who's a conservative.
Now, back to the IFF article. They call themselves "nonpartisan" and in the very next breath say party affiliation tends to predict how someone scores on their index. Well, pick a lane.
Their "blue wave" chart also counts Brad Little's shrinking margin as a loss. Now, I mostly agree with them on Little. He lets refugees flood our state and goes hard for Idaho Launch, which is a de facto socialist wealth redistribution program. My critiques of him are many. But you can't spend years telling everybody he's the problem and then cry when fewer people vote for him.
Idaho curb-stomped Prop 1. To act like a 12-point win is a disappointment is grasping at straws. It was a double-digit proper ass-kicking and Idaho should be proud of the work we did.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c310d90b-d96f-43b2-9fbe-66ec867b3dea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then there's the shout-out to Johnstone, Hyde (and Crowder). Out of every Republican who lost this year, these are the ones who get a name check? The IFF co-founder, their PAC guy, and the whole inner circle lined up behind them. But they were running in Biden country, and everybody knew they were gonna lose. So why call them "missed opportunities"? These were never real opportunities.
I think the real problem is that IFF wants to be two things at once. Read their own priority list in their article: taxes and limiting government come first, and "traditional Idaho values" come last. They put out a "Freedom and Family Agenda," then their index knocks a bill protecting orphans and gives a shrug to one punishing employers who hire illegals.
_**This is what happens when you view a nation as an economy instead of a people.**_
And it's the starkest difference between libertarianism and conservatism. When you have libertarians scoring and rating bills, traditional family values, the border, and protecting kids always take the back seat.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f848c0-d0b8-4125-bdee-8c72a7106d33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Because libertarians just want government out of the way so everybody can do whatever they want (e.g. open drugs, rampant prostitution, open borders, weapons for illegals, etc.). But conservatives want to protect borders, language, and culture first, _even when that means the government has to do something._ Now, those two can and do overlap. But when they don't, IFF picks the libertarian side.
Even the article can't decide what it is.
The Prop 1 section says "Praise God for this win!" Then it closes by listing what IFF stands for:_ "limited government, fiscal responsibility, individual liberty, and constitutional governance." _God and family don't make the final list.
Their "wake-up call" says as much. They said this election "should be a wake-up call for all freedom and liberty-minded folks in Idaho." Freedom folks. Liberty folks. But not a word about conservative folks.
(Chase two rabbits and you lose both)
For the record, Idaho came through just fine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b396094-ba56-4040-a260-9ea3dd030239?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sure, we lost a few seats, but look around.
Republicans lost supermajorities in Utah, Missouri, Kansas, Ohio, Indiana, South Carolina, Arkansas and Florida. _Arizona Republicans lost the whole legislature for the first time in 60 years._ Texas elected a Democrat governor and James Talarico.
_But we kept our Republican supermajority in both chambers, held every statewide office, and passed the bill I carried in the Senate to put English in the Idaho Constitution as our official language._
Yes, there's always work to do. Always.
**But the blue wave skipped Idaho.**
So don't let anybody's cliff's-edge talk get to you. It's easy to get blackpilled and retreat into despair, but we need to fight that urge. The doomer crowd is a wet blanket on conservatives.
Throw it off and live in hope. Then fight for what's right: borders, language, culture, and your family.

clean_body: Here's a post-election breakdown from the Idaho Freedom Foundation, which a lot of people in the state follow. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Nov 10 | | | | | | | | | | | | Here's , which a lot of people in the state follow. Go read it first, then come back to this article. Okay, you read it? Good. First off, look at where their "conservative losses" came from. By their own admission, it was last May's primary. But Democrats didn't vote in the 2026 Idaho Republican primary. Republicans did. So lumping the loss of IFF's loyalists (who use the Freedom Index as their voting guide) into a blue-wave story is disingenuous at best because there was no blue wave in the 2026 Republican primary. It's nonsensical. Now, IFF gets a lot right, especially on spending and fiscal issues. I scored 78% on their index this year. But look at what they call a "conservative": anyone who scores well on their "Freedom Index." That's how they pick winners and losers. This is the same index that rated a bill making it a crime to hire illegals a big fat ZERO (HB 700, 2026). It gave the same zero rating to a bill making AI child porn a felony (HB 465, 2024), basically hinting that it was a victimless crime. This is the same index that rated a bill saying the state can't steal from orphans as negative this year (HB 558, 2026), and the same index that rated a bill to get junk food out of EBT as bad too (HB 109, 2025). I could go on but you get the point. | | ---|---|--- To be fair, IFF isn't the only one doing this type of thing. It seems like everybody in this state has a scorecard of sorts, and everybody has an agenda. IACI (basically the Chamber of Commerce at the state level) only scores like 12 bills a year based on what its corporate members want, and I'm near the bottom of their favs list. Their PAC even backs leadership who fail their own scorecard, then goes after conservatives who score well. Makes no sense. Farm Bureau has one too. They say they want a secure border, but when the bills to crack down on hiring illegals died this year, they didn't shed a tear (their lobbyist said E-Verify is the feds' job). Idaho Business for Education has one too. Back in 2021, 18 of the 19 Democrats in the Legislature scored a perfect 100 on it. Point is that scorecards are a dime a dozen. You just have to do some digging to find out what each one is really pushing before you let it tell you who's a conservative. Now, back to the IFF article. They call themselves "nonpartisan" and in the very next breath say party affiliation tends to predict how someone scores on their index. Well, pick a lane. Their "blue wave" chart also counts Brad Little's shrinking margin as a loss. Now, I mostly agree with them on Little. He lets refugees flood our state and goes hard for Idaho Launch, which is a de facto socialist wealth redistribution program. My critiques of him are many. But you can't spend years telling everybody he's the problem and then cry when fewer people vote for him. Idaho curb-stomped Prop 1. To act like a 12-point win is a disappointment is grasping at straws. It was a double-digit proper ass-kicking and Idaho should be proud of the work we did. | | ---|---|--- Then there's the shout-out to Johnstone, Hyde (and Crowder). Out of every Republican who lost this year, these are the ones who get a name check? The IFF co-founder, their PAC guy, and the whole inner circle lined up behind them. But they were running in Biden country, and everybody knew they were gonna lose. So why call them "missed opportunities"? These were never real opportunities. I think the real problem is that IFF wants to be two things at once. Read their own priority list in their article: taxes and limiting government come first, and "traditional Idaho values" come last. They put out a "Freedom and Family Agenda," then their index knocks a bill protecting orphans and gives a shrug to one punishing employers who hire illegals. This is what happens when you view a nation as an economy instead of a people. And it's the starkest difference between libertarianism and conservatism. When you have libertarians scoring and rating bills, traditional family values, the border, and protecting kids always take the back seat. | | ---|---|--- Because libertarians just want government out of the way so everybody can do whatever they want (e.g. open drugs, rampant prostitution, open borders, weapons for illegals, etc.). But conservatives want to protect borders, language, and culture first, even when that means the government has to do something. Now, those two can and do overlap. But when they don't, IFF picks the libertarian side. Even the article can't decide what it is. The Prop 1 section says "Praise God for this win!" Then it closes by listing what IFF stands for: "limited government, fiscal responsibility, individual liberty, and constitutional governance." God and family don't make the final list. Their "wake-up call" says as much. They said this election "should be a wake-up call for all freedom and liberty-minded folks in Idaho." Freedom folks. Liberty folks. But not a word about conservative folks. (Chase two rabbits and you lose both) For the record, Idaho came through just fine. | | ---|---|--- Sure, we lost a few seats, but look around. Republicans lost supermajorities in Utah, Missouri, Kansas, Ohio, Indiana, South Carolina, Arkansas and Florida. Arizona Republicans lost the whole legislature for the first time in 60 years. Texas elected a Democrat governor and James Talarico. But we kept our Republican supermajority in both chambers, held every statewide office, and passed the bill I carried in the Senate to put English in the Idaho Constitution as our official language. Yes, there's always work to do. Always. But the blue wave skipped Idaho. So don't let anybody's cliff's-edge talk get to you. It's easy to get blackpilled and retreat into despair, but we need to fight that urge. The doomer crowd is a wet blanket on conservatives. Throw it off and live in hope. Then fight for what's right: borders, language, culture, and your family. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Brian Lenney ? ?

The rule I learned in the SEAL teams is simple: When you’re in a tough fight, you don't leave your teammate hanging. You show up, and you have their back. [ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

We need to impeach Pete Hegseth, NOW. And it could happen THIS WEEK!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40022?source=email-20261110&t=1011&akid=11572%2E5885482%2ETxB_a6 ]Headline: Rep. Thomas Massie moves to force vote on Hegseth impeachment

Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) introduced a privileged resolution charging the
Defense Secretary with multiple serious violations of law and the
Constitution. Then, in September, Speaker Mike Johnson sent lawmakers home
early to try to stop the vote. Now lawmakers are back in Washington, and
the impeachment resolution could come up for a vote as soon as TOMORROW.

This vote could pass. Both Democrats and even some Republicans have had
enough of Trump and Hegseth’s illegal, costly, and unpopular war with
Iran. So now we need to make sure every member of Congress understands
that their constituents are watching — and we have just 24 hours to do it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40022?source=email-20261110&t=1012&akid=11572%2E5885482%2ETxB_a6 ]ADD YOUR NAME NOW: Tell your Representative to support the articles of
impeachment against Pete Hegseth and demand accountability.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40022?source=email-20261110&t=1013&akid=11572%2E5885482%2ETxB_a6 ]ADD YOUR NAME

Hegseth launched an illegal war on Iran, ordered extrajudicial killings
off the coast of South America, dismantled the departments responsible for
protecting civilians, and retaliated against Sen. Mark Kelly for speaking
out about unlawful military orders.

Even Republicans are making their anger at Hegseth clear, with a
Republican member of Congress telling Fox News that Hegseth doesn't have
"a lot of love" on Capitol Hill. And if the House passes the impeachment
resolution, the Senate will have to start an impeachment trial — forcing
Hegseth to answer for his warmongering.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40022?source=email-20261110&t=1014&akid=11572%2E5885482%2ETxB_a6 ]Headline: Republicans with 'little left to lose' poised to doom Hegseth
to impeachment soon: Axios

Public opinion is clear: two-thirds of voters who supported Democrats in
2024 and 20% of Republicans support impeaching Hegseth. That's why we're
mobilizing our grassroots network to make sure Congress hears from
constituents before this vote.

We have just 24 hours before the vote and need to OVERWHELM Congress with
calls to impeach Hegseth, now!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40022?source=email-20261110&t=1015&akid=11572%2E5885482%2ETxB_a6 ]Send your Representative a message now: investigate the allegations,
uphold Congress's constitutional responsibilities, and impeach Hegseth
NOW!

When we organize, we win.

Our communities have waited decades for this. clean_body: If one more member of Congress signs before November 12, the Dream & Promise Act gets a House vote. | | | Peter, this is it. We have less than two days to get ONE more member of Congress to sign the discharge petition and force a House vote on the Dream and Promise Act — legislation that would create a pathway to citizenship for millions of DACA recipients, immigrant youth, TPS holders, and people with Deferred Enforced Departure (DED). Our communities have waited decades for this. We’ve built careers, raised families, and kept this country running, all while knowing our protections could be taken away at any moment. If just one more member of Congress adds their name before November 12, it goes to a House vote.If not, the window for a vote this session closes. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | We're almost there. Peter,
Something I’ve been really proud of over the last week has been the rest of the country learning a thing or two about Mississippi and who we are. We are a beautiful state with wonderful people.
**Mississippi matters. Everybody better get used to hearing that.**
Last week, hundreds of thousands of voters in all 82 counties came together to say they wanted to pick a senator who represented _THEM,_ not the billionaires.
We owe it to them to make sure that the rest of this process plays out smoothly.
We need to count every lawful vote, and protect the will of the people. I’m so proud of all our team has done so far to make that happen, but there’s still a lot of work in front of us – and we have serious budget needs we have to meet.
I will always stand up and fight for Mississippi. Now, for just a little bit longer, I’m asking you to stand with me.
[**Can you please make a split donation of $10 or even $25 between our campaign and Abdul El-Sayed to help us win the Mississippi Senate race? Friends, I'm back in the arena, and I'm not stepping back in halfway. I'm all in. Michigan and America's greatest asset has never been a politician, a party, or a pile of money. clean_body: | | | Dear Peter, 100% of OLCV's priority candidates in the 2026 general election have won! That's right. Oregon just delivered BIG wins for climate action, clean energy, and environmental protection. Together, we elected climate champions, protected critical legislative seats, and built momentum for a healthier, more affordable future. But winning elections is just the beginning. Now comes the work of making sure our leaders deliver. In the months ahead, OLCV will be: Holding elected officials accountable to their climate and environmental promises. Fighting for clean energy solutions that lower costs for Oregon families. Holding powerful corporations accountable. Protecting Oregon's land, water, wildlife, and public health. And monthly giving is a win-win: More accessible for you: Spread your support throughout the year with a smaller, manageable gift each month. More powerful for Oregon: Reliable monthly contributions help OLCV plan ahead and put more resources directly toward the work of protecting our environment and electing climate champions. Plus, when you join OLCV's Sustainer Circle, you'll get special insider benefits, including: Our monthly e-newsletter with updates on the fights and victories you're helping make possible. Our election report, sharing the impact of our work at the ballot box. Our annual environmental scorecard, showing how Oregon's elected leaders measure up. Don't let the momentum stop on Election Day. Become a monthly donor today!Your monthly commitment will help turn this year's incredible victories into lasting progress for Oregon.** Together, we can keep Oregon moving forward. One month, one victory, and one big step at a time. Yall, the South had something to say at the ballot box last week — and we can’t ignore it.
Georgia just elected the nation’s first Black woman governor in Keisha Lance Bottoms. We drove record turnout at the polls. And we delivered a decisive Senate win in one of the country’s closest races.
**_This_****is what happens when the Democratic Party invests in Black voters. And that’s why we need to keep expanding on these investments to build an infrastructure that engages Black voters all year long — not just when there’s an election on the horizon.**
****[**I launched the Building Lasting Alliances for Impact and Results (BLAIR) PAC because when Democrats target Black voters with Black messaging, Black leaders, and an agenda that addresses the needs of Black communities, we win. Will you become a founding donor to my BLAIR PAC so we can expand on this year’s historic wins and change the future of Black voter turnout for years to come?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqunzgRltChG2pxSiGGQC3Y8E-i-nTf33AciI82zXU9mUNuxebBwzuB_YDiWUlQYcj6OGgL7XaqIlVFveZHVlYtcJvd0a9w3tchkbdqyCFK9SN08rYiTP8gwZnF9ZblkPUzRqXbh_cZOu9QI2J4Kb_oUXwXX_HoVBzedhuDv_-dW6os7y3a5jB1kCGQXwzCBpUhijlXVk_8laZvEEUVb4avcFxCDRPt4PKNohBweFD3VF0mPQJRLvOhs7HvHPj4PUmZn1RYF_iQcbDA5tuWSmBo7XCHHoFC10t_NfAhMmEPci7OqnrRUcaJMtOEApDeBy8bS7Yz2Pz-thC-cA9Eg5b7lIlRAGimCwwLaSrFoPgjFbF8BC9_WNdBws2dG0mfIL_P71gFWH64SuWvVXGuzGWv6/4vm/yLBdsSmETpiaRjA7uEHoYw/h1/h001.SM039Rj10Ls3bxWS5hNk9H995B-pg5gnkUXZLfI0Ba4)****

Republicans spent the better part of this year working to drain the power of Black voters. They gerrymandered our districts, weakened our voting rights, and used the full force of their majority control to try to silence us.
But in battleground Southern states like Georgia, Black voters drove the blue tsunami. Black voters shattered turnout records. **And Black voters proved that**** _we_****are the vanguards of change in this country.**
If there’s one lesson that Democrats _must_ take from this election, it’s that the power of Black voters can’t be taken for granted.
Over the next two years, my BLAIR PAC will continue engaging Black voters, working with leaders in Congress to build a Black economic agenda, and fighting to expand the coalition of voters we’ve worked decades to build.
**[With your help, we can fill a major gap in the national Democratic infrastructure and build upon this November’s historic wins year after year after year. # [Fake food truck steals $11.4M in Nvidia AI hardware](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Six pallets of **[Nvidia hardware reportedly worth $11.4 million disappeared after pickup](https://substack.com/redirect/d6d67e4e-c3fa-47f1-bc5f-80acb4361a32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d6d67e4e-c3fa-47f1-bc5f-80acb4361a32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in Oakland on August 29, and as of November 9 Oakland police had announced no arrests or recovery while a Berkeley professor warned the gear could reach China.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Pickup and disappearance:** A truck bearing a food company's logo took the load on August 29, headed south, stopped for hours at a time, and was last tracked in San Bernardino County.
* **Police timeline:** The buyers reported the shipment missing in early September; Oakland police logged a grand-theft report on September 13 and have not identified the cargo, owner, shipper, carrier, or driver.
* **Expert warning:** UC Berkeley's Olaf Groth told ABC News the missing chips are a national-security concern because "we don't know where these chips are going. They could be going to China."
* **Broader pattern:** More than $100 million in similar shipments have been stolen since June, and the FBI's April advisory put 2025 U.S.-Canada cargo-theft losses near $725 million, up 60% from 2024.

# [Nvidia board probes Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's **[board opened an independent investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/4f659f63-6853-4c60-9687-04463b1bef54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4f659f63-6853-4c60-9687-04463b1bef54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence believes was working for Beijing, while shareholders sued and Trump said the FBI is looking into it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Board probe launched:** The independent directors hired outside counsel after Huang admitted unfaithfulness; the board said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised and that Huang is cooperating.
* **Class action filed:**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/19269c3b-6e09-470c-95f1-4f86c73962af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Shareholders sued Huang and Nvidia on Tuesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/19269c3b-6e09-470c-95f1-4f86c73962af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** alleging they were misled about the relationship with the accused Chinese spy.
* **Trump and FBI:** Trump said Huang told him Monday[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/126880a5-349b-40fe-8317-831c679cae6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[he did not know she was a spy](https://substack.com/redirect/6e1c25b0-7615-40ff-87cd-d539fc70d1ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/126880a5-349b-40fe-8317-831c679cae6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and that he believes him; the president added the FBI is looking into it.
* **Market reaction:** Nvidia fell more than 5% Monday and continued lower Tuesday, yet the rest of the Magnificent 7[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/994aa153-ee9f-4123-8987-40ee4e7424cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[held up as the broader market bounced](https://substack.com/redirect/994aa153-ee9f-4123-8987-40ee4e7424cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.

# [Hot October CPI seals case for December rate hike](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
October consumer **[prices rose 0.4% and core prices 0.3%,](https://substack.com/redirect/13a80ff0-2073-485d-817a-3479ef6984d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** both hotter than expected, with no year-over-year rates available because of last year's shutdown, as Fed Governor Waller **[said a 50 bp December hike should be considered.](https://substack.com/redirect/a763f264-443e-4868-a1d2-1d397ddb4ff6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Print details:** Headline CPI increased 0.4% month-over-month versus 0.3% expected; core rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected.
* **No annual figures:** The BLS never collected October 2025 prices during the shutdown, so traders focused solely on the month-over-month readings.
* **Waller signal:** The governor said he is **[leaning toward a December increase](https://substack.com/redirect/1a160886-def4-4b25-a330-25980c0fd630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and that a 50 bp move should be considered if core printed around 0.3% or higher.
* **Market pricing:** 25 bp odds jumped above 99% while the chance of a 50 bp hike rose to roughly 14%, and stocks lost steam.
