# [Anthropic prices IPO at $70-78 for up to $1.4T valuation](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic filed an amended S-1 seeking **[825 million shares at $70 to $78,](https://substack.com/redirect/dbd9a2b2-1790-4cb5-90ba-c7ef63e2ed4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** implying **[roughly $1.0 trillion or up to $1.4 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/fc8f512e-0b05-46fd-b9f4-ae8126174b89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** fully diluted, while launching cheaper Fable models as its roadshow begins.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal size:** The offering plus a $26 billion supplier placement and greenshoe pushes the raise above $100 billion.
* **Valuation range:** The implied market value sits **[30-50% below the $2 trillion figure floated earlier.](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1533f3-756e-4ebd-a7fe-df7dcf911711?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Model update:** Claude Fable 5.2 was priced 20% below its predecessor at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output.
* **Timing:** The roadshow starts Tuesday, **[with pricing expected around Nov. 18](https://substack.com/redirect/90c63c22-db31-4bed-bdf6-11bab667944d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and trading targeted for Nov. 19.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/c4966de2-f7e7-4456-8df2-d3077291d1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Monday's record bounce hits inflation wall on Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Dow soared 1,132 points and the Nasdaq jumped nearly 3% on Monday as chip stocks rallied while Nvidia fell,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3db212ef-caf3-4e66-a83c-3a8f4db7dae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[only for hotter CPI data to stall the rebound on Tuesday.](https://substack.com/redirect/3db212ef-caf3-4e66-a83c-3a8f4db7dae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Monday surge:** Amazon and Tesla led the charge **[as dip buyers returned and the S&P erased post-election losses.](https://substack.com/redirect/fd3c089a-5796-4b35-974a-bfaf69e92df4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Nvidia exception:** Nvidia dropped nearly 5% on the Huang news even as the rest of the market enjoyed its best day in months.
* **Tuesday reversal:** Futures and cash indexes lost steam once the 0.4% CPI print boosted December hike odds.
* **Rotation noted:** Money moved out of AI names even **[as broader indexes held some of Monday's gains.](https://substack.com/redirect/ecff6e0d-4b3e-4cd2-a5de-c32cc68b16a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/c4966de2-f7e7-4456-8df2-d3077291d1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Goldman: 35 GW of 2027 data centers already committed](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman argues the 35 GW of data-center additions planned for 2027 **[are largely already under construction](https://substack.com/redirect/27b6bda0-d21a-4c1d-b460-874ebc9cbe37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and still sees $1.3 trillion in AI infrastructure capex by 2027, **[even as a bipartisan permitting bill advances.](https://substack.com/redirect/8673f424-524e-4182-9f49-c890e518ed06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Buildout locked in:** The bank says restrictions on new permits do not stop projects already underway.
* **Capex view holds:** Goldman maintains its $1.3 trillion AI infrastructure spending forecast through 2027.
* **Permitting progress:** The Senate voted 73-25 to advance a bill that would **[make data centers pay incremental grid costs](https://substack.com/redirect/8de327af-6bce-4631-a169-e3a2ddef7280?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and shorten NEPA suit windows to 150 days.
* **Texas share:** Texas accounts for more than a quarter of planned U.S. data-center capacity additions through 2030.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/c4966de2-f7e7-4456-8df2-d3077291d1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# Goldman flags AI disconnect after extreme chip washout
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 25% since October on AI-spending fears, yet **[Goldman argues the market is pricing a slowdown that is not occurring](https://substack.com/redirect/f018ef49-81e1-40ba-ab20-b2281dcf257e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f018ef49-81e1-40ba-ab20-b2281dcf257e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while 35 GW of 2027 capacity is already being built.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e7cc50e-9e98-4917-8679-575949466134?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Drawdown scale:** SOX recorded[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8c824dfa-44fe-4921-991a-a2bfc41245e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[one of its most extreme drawdowns on record](https://substack.com/redirect/8c824dfa-44fe-4921-991a-a2bfc41245e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and remains well below its 200-day average.
* **Goldman view:** The bank says moratorium talk misses committed projects and still forecasts $1.3 trillion in AI capex by 2027.
* **Monday bounce:** Chip stocks **[soared Monday even as Nvidia sold off,](https://substack.com/redirect/206b56e2-1525-4060-92f7-372416a8a9e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** leaving the SOX up 5%.
* **Positioning washed:** Allocations have fallen back toward year lows after the five-day performance through Thursday was the worst since Covid.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/c4966de2-f7e7-4456-8df2-d3077291d1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Trump downplays Iran strikes and oil falls below $90](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Brent crude fell 2.6% to $90.20 and briefly traded under $90 on Tuesday after **[President Trump said](https://substack.com/redirect/9467dc07-7cc2-4397-a2fa-0c267b049401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9467dc07-7cc2-4397-a2fa-0c267b049401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)military action against Iran **[did not seem necessary at this point](https://substack.com/redirect/6e35ac18-d6ec-4b1a-905a-21ffca49d140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/6e35ac18-d6ec-4b1a-905a-21ffca49d140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and that the war was going to end fairly soon.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Price move:** The drop extended Monday's losses as Hormuz shipping **[showed signs of recovery.](https://substack.com/redirect/29cecdf1-a180-46c4-84db-0f3718f5964a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Trump comments:** The president said Iran militarily is effectively over and kept the door open but played down new strikes.
* **War premium fade:** Analysts noted the steepest one-day drop since April after the midterm results as hedge funds had already dumped $6.6 billion in Brent.
* **Still fragile:** Some desks caution that a lasting peace deal remains unlikely despite the de-escalation talk.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/c4966de2-f7e7-4456-8df2-d3077291d1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Credit markets: chipmakers now riskier than hyperscalers](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman's credit desk said chip **[Credit Default Swapss blew out wider than hyperscaler spreads](https://substack.com/redirect/1e9a466d-179f-4a38-a7ae-f4a996dd56d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the first time as AI default-swap volumes hit a record and risk migrated down the supply chain.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2698c9b4-e03a-4d07-b5c3-4a6f5ea4cd12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Spread flip:** Chip credit default swaps moved wider than those of the large cloud operators that buy their products.
* **Index calm:** CDX Investment Grade widened only 3.5 basis points even after Thursday's sharp equity drop.
* **Issuance absorbed:** The market digested $296 billion of hyperscaler debt this year against a $250 billion forecast, with more queued for 2027.
* **Goldman warning:** The bank said the broad index is hiding the damage concentrated in AI-related names.

My name was on the ballot, but this victory belongs to all of us. And the only way we can make real change is if I know what YOUR priorities, concerns, and hopes for the future are. I wish I could talk to each of you personally, but until I can be in 100 places at once, surveys like this are genuinely the next best thing. That’s why I’m reaching out to hear from you directly: | | Together, we won Ohio by almost 5 full points, flipped the Senate, and stared down Donald Trump’s billionaires and corporate special interests and collectively told them, “Not in Ohio.” But this victory doesn’t put us at the finish line. Our work is just getting started. We’re going to fight to lower costs and make life better for working families. My staff and I are more fired up than ever to deliver for the people of Ohio. We can do this. But I need to know what’s most important to you. That’s why I’m checking in today, and I’m really hopeful you will take a minute to fill out our short survey. | | Thank you for making your voice heard. Thank you for standing with me. ---
Thank you for helping make me the next Congressperson for Michigan’s 11th district.
It’s the honor of my lifetime to serve the people of Michigan. We sent a message that we’re ready to take our fight from Oakland County to the halls of Congress. That Michigan needs a new generation of leaders who will be bolder, tougher, and stronger.
Our campaign has always been about standing up for you and standing up to the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration. The reckless and dangerous decisions from Washington have increased costs on Michigan families and eroded the core functions of our democracy.
Enough is enough.
I’m taking with me a record of expanding civil rights, safeguarding our voting systems, enacting new gun safety laws, protecting reproductive freedom, and making sure our economy works for everyone.
On top of that, we broke barriers – I’m proud to be the first openly gay member of Congress in Michigan history.
I am deeply grateful to every voter, volunteer, and supporter who made this historic victory possible. To my family and friends, the grassroots activists who fueled this campaign, the local officials who were in my corner, the labor unions who can count on me, the LGBTQ groups who fight for representation, and many more.
Thank you for believing in this campaign. I am excited to get to work on behalf of the people of the 11th Congressional District.
Jeremy

On top of that, we broke barriers – I’m proud to be the first openly gay member of Congress in Michigan history. I am deeply grateful to every voter, volunteer, and supporter who made this historic victory possible. To my family and friends, the grassroots activists who fueled this campaign, the local officials who were in my corner, the labor unions who can count on me, the LGBTQ groups who fight for representation, and many more. Thank you for believing in this campaign. I am excited to get to work on behalf of the people of the 11th Congressional District. | | Across the country, the American people sent a clear message, resoundingly rejecting Trump's — and his party's — "families lose, billionaires win" agenda. Americans rejected Trump's massive cost increases that are pressing families to the wall. Americans rejected his mile-deep swamp of corruption. And Americans rejected Trump's shredding of our democratic republic as he worked to establish a strongman state. But it wouldn't have happened without each and every one of you who got involved in this election. You volunteered, you walked, you talked, you donated. To every one of you who helped my campaign — or helped my effort to boost other campaigns — a massive thank you from my heart. What you have achieved is extraordinary. You flipped about 50 House seats. You flipped 7 Senate seats — and maybe 9!! Onward, Mary Peltola and Scott Colom! That is an outcome beyond anything we could have hoped for. Together, we are fighting to build a better world, and I am grateful for your partnership in the battle. Now, Congress has to deliver. We campaigned on costs, corruption, and saving our republic. I still have the textbook from my freshman year Econ 101 course. It's called _Principles of Economics_ , and it remains one of the most popular introductory economics textbooks out there. My wife, always looking to declutter, has asked several times if we could get rid of it. But the material in this thing is just too bonkers to part with. Here's a not-unusual passage from the book, in a section labeled "Price Increases after Natural Disasters."
> If you want to score points cracking down on mean, greedy profiteers, pushing anti-'gouging' rules is a very good thing. But if you're one of the people the law 'protects' from 'price gouging,' you won't fare as well. Consider this scenario: You are thirsty--worried that your baby is going to become dehydrated. You ... finally find that dreaded monster, the price gouger. He offers a bottle of water that cost $1 last week at an 'outrageous' price--say $20. You pay it to survive the disaster. You resent the price gouger. But if he hadn't demanded $20, he'd have been out of water. It was the price gouger's 'exploitation' that saved your child.
This was not an explicitly rightwing textbook--just the ostensibly neutral resource for an intro economics course at a liberal university. The fact that so much of it reads like an Ayn Rand novel reflects the reality of mainstream economics today--a field that claims to be based on scientific principles but in actuality functions as rank, market fundamentalist ideology.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=223215686&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzMjE1Njg2LCJpYXQiOjE3OTQzMzc4MzksImV4cCI6MTc5NjkyOTgzOSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.YHszq7vkDEUR2mlaP3nKQxV3WMuVjuNQNjrLkFXjLsA)
_Anti-Fascist Economics_ , by Isabella Weber, represents an urgently-needed challenge to this orthodoxy--an orthodoxy that Weber, an economics professor at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, argues has fueled the rise of the authoritarian far right in recent years.
As her book makes clear, this is not a new argument, but rather one rooted in a rich tradition. Karl Polanyi, the seminal economic historian, coined the phrase "the fascist virus" to describe the claim by orthodox economics that the "laws of the market economy prohibit any intervention in economic life on the part of the working people." To paraphrase, when people are suffering, and their democratic leaders' response is to say, _Oh well, that 's the market for you, nothing we can do about it_, that is rocket fuel for fascists, who can in turn argue, _Look, democracy isn 't solving your problems, take a chance with us._
Nobody had a better practical understanding of this principle than Franklin Roosevelt. Weber describes how, to launch the New Deal, Roosevelt had to break with orthodox economics--indeed, Roosevelt once said, "I took economics courses in college, and everything I was taught was wrong." Roosevelt defined fascism as "the growth of private power to a point where it becomes stronger than the democratic state itself," and warned that "People who are hungry and out of a job are the stuff of which dictatorships are made." Put this way, the antidote to fascism becomes obvious: mobilize the state to contain corporate power and provide people with economic security--the exact kinds of interventions that market fundamentalists guarantee will lead to disaster.
But Roosevelt's New Deal did not lead to disaster. It was fabulously successful at stamping out the fascist sentiments that were gaining ground in the United States, just as they were in Germany and elsewhere in the early 1930s. Indeed, the New Deal made Roosevelt the most popular president we've ever had. And his administration's direction of industrial outputs and prices during World War II--through the War Production Board and the Office of Price Administration--was so effective that living standards for Americans actually rose during wartime, an unheard-of achievement.
For a few decades, at least, it became almost impossible to argue with a straight face that the state can't act to improve outcomes for common people--because everyone had just collectively experienced it doing exactly that. But this consensus was attacked, weakened, and ultimately displaced over the following half-century by Polanyi's fascist virus. Perhaps the best embodiment of this new market fundamentalism was Friedrich Hayek's _The Road to Serfdom,_ which was published in 1944 and became a bible for right-wing movements in the 1970s and right-wing governments in the 1980s _._ Hayek makes a classic slippery slope argument, insisting that the only legitimate role for the state is to enforce our subordination to the market--which in practice means subordination to the owners of capital--as any further intervention will lead inevitably toward totalitarianism. As John Maynard Keynes, the most famous economist of his day, wrote in a letter to Hayek after reading _The Road to Serfdom_ in 1944, "You are trying to persuade us that so soon as one moves an inch in the planned direction you are necessarily launched on the slippery path which will lead you in due course over the precipice."
This is, of course, kindergarten-level reasoning: _If you do one little thing I don 't like, the whole world will end._ But it's an extremely convenient analytical framework for economic elites, who do not want democratic states horning in on their God-given right to control our jobs, our lives, and our society. And so--starting as a partisan revolution under Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the 1980s, and solidifying as a bipartisan consensus under Tony Blair and Bill Clinton in the 1990s--this kindergarten-level approach to the world became an unquestionable economic orthodoxy, so indisputable in elite circles that the authors of "neutral" Econ 101 textbooks could wax poetic about disaster profiteering and think nothing of it.
This provides a precise explanation for why, when fascism once again raised its ugly head in the 21st century, the United States--in marked contrast to its resilient response in the 1930s--failed to avoid a spiral into far-right authoritarianism. First there was President Obama's tepid "banks got bailed out, we got sold out" response to the 2008 financial crisis, which Weber argues helped lead to Trump I. And then--the real focus of Weber's book--was President Biden's refusal to take action to stabilize the price of essential goods following the supply shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to Trump II. As Weber puts it:
> The Biden administration faced a basic choice: It could brush aside what people were saying about the severe problems they were facing and instead lean into how "great" the macroeconomy was doing and lament that there was nothing to be done about inflation, or it could take action to address the affordability and inequality crisis by disciplining capital. For the most part, it chose the first route.
Weber catalogues how, across thousands of public earnings calls with shareholders, corporate leaders celebrated that supply chain dislocations from the pandemic were giving them license to hike prices and make obscene windfall profits. Often these statements were phrased in technical terms: Dupont reported that supply shocks were creating a "constructive market for pricing"; General Mills explained to shareholders that inflation would allow the company to "realize net pricing." But sometimes they dispensed with that language--as one CEO told investors, "It's kind of like a rain dance, I pray for inflation every day I come to work because inflation, our top line is really driven by inflation."
Despite these literal confessions of "greedflation," a term Weber coined to describe how companies were exploiting inflation to score excessive profits, the Biden administration, under the influence of establishment economists, chose to treat inflation like an unknowable act of God--something that could not possibly be addressed with specific government interventions, beyond the sacrifice-the-poor sledgehammer of rate hikes and austerity.
The one counterexample to this trend is itself extremely illustrative. In August 2024, in her first campaign speech on economic policy after taking over the Democratic presidential ticket, Kamala Harris proposed a federal ban on price gouging for food. The plan polled extremely well with swing voters, but it was immediately assailed by leading economists. Jason Furman, who served as chair of the Council of Economic Advisors under President Obama, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/afb44c47-2814-415f-8b32-59917f7d5ba9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the _New York Times_ , "This is not sensible policy ... There's no upside here." In the runup to an election that would have existential stakes for American democracy, where the cost of essential goods was the number one concern for voters, Democratic-aligned economists were actively working to stop the Democratic nominee from giving working class Americans a reason to vote for her. Whether Harris was more influenced by economists like Furman or by her billionaire donors, who also [protested](https://substack.com/redirect/563b2643-ad13-4904-a3a9-432bc603e137?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the price gouging ban, is hard to say. What's clear is that Harris dropped the issue. The campaign ad that focused on her price gouging proposal, which scored extremely well in focus groups, was hardly ever aired.
What is perhaps the most frustrating aspect of this story, as Weber highlights, is that everyone involved in both the Biden administration and the Harris campaign had a remarkably clear template, right across the border, for how to block Trump's return to power. Mexico's former president--popularly referred to by his initials, AMLO--ignored mainstream economists' insistence that there was nothing the state could do to stabilize prices. In the face of pandemic-era inflation, his government developed a program to fix the total price of a basket of 24 essentials--mostly food staples like rice and vegetable oil, along with hygiene essentials like toilet paper and soap. Companies could choose how to meet the overall cost cap, so long as all the items together did not exceed the total basket price. Every Monday, AMLO held a press conference on the essentials basket, praising firms that offered particularly inexpensive baskets and calling out those charging the most--thereby creating a public relations incentive for companies to toe the line, while ensuring that every Mexican family knew that their president was fighting on their behalf to keep prices low.
AMLO ended his term with a sky-high 70 percent approval rating. His mentee and successor, Claudia Sheinbaum, won Mexico's June, 2024 election in a historic landslide. She continued AMLO's essentials basket program, and two years into her term touts an approval rating that regularly [reaches](https://substack.com/redirect/77ca83db-8a93-41ca-8c0d-b0b4a3b9ae90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 75 percent.
Instead of dismissing Americans' affordability concerns as a "vibecession," imagine if the Biden administration had established a program similar to that of AMLO and Sheinbaum. Imagine if every Monday Biden--or, considering his cognitive and communicative deficits, Biden and Harris together--had held a press conference reporting on costs and calling out price gougers. Or, to take an even more recent example, imagine if, during her campaign, Harris had passed or called for measures to clear the debt of millions of workers, reduce the maximum workweek, and establish zero-fare public transportation, as [Brazil's President Lula did](https://substack.com/redirect/c457c865-4c24-43af-8a6e-acbfdada6b44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the lead-up to his momentous come-from-behind victory over FIavio Bolsonaro. It's difficult for me to envision Democrats losing to Trump in that universe. Who's going to get taken in by Trump's infamous [grocery store](https://substack.com/redirect/ab46e878-accb-4422-af41-136516ece1f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) campaign stunt when Democrats are demonstrating to the American people that they are actually fighting to take on corporate profiteers and bring down the costs of essentials?
Weber describes additional policy proposals that constitute what she calls an "economics of essentials." These include shorter-term solutions to stabilize key supply chains that everyone depends on, such as public buffer stocks for essential commodities, in the vein of China's grain buffer stock system, which held domestic prices stable against global food inflation, or its National Fertilizer Commercial Reserve, which sheltered Chinese farmers against fertilizer price spikes. Weber also stresses that short-term stabilization must always be in service of longer-term solutions that attack the root causes of inflation, and places decarbonization--replacing shock-prone fossil fuels with stable renewables--as the most urgent of these. "As long as fossil fuel prices are allowed to explode, yielding the record profits we have witnessed in recent energy crises, it will be very difficult to convince investors to move out of the sector," she writes, recommending a permanent excess profits tax to ensure that profits in the fossil fuel sector never exceed a certain threshold and an emergency price ceiling to prevent wholesale prices from shooting beyond a certain level.
These ideas represent a desperately important corrective to the Jason Furmans of the world--elite economists whose smug dismissal of government action for the public good has aided in bringing far-right authoritarianism roaring back in the United States and across the globe. _Anti-Fascist Economics_ demonstrates why we cannot listen to these voices anymore--not only because market fundamentalism is a severe threat to democracy, but also, it's worth stating, because their view of the world is _extremely dumb_.
Take that passage from _Principles of Economics_. It's set in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. The passage declares that critics of price gouging "just don't understand basic economics," and that if you just "let the market work, suppliers will come." But the supply shock after Hurricane Katrina had an actual cause: Transportation infrastructure was destroyed. Roads and railways and ports were swept away by the storm. The greedy price-gouger wasn't inducing new supplies to enter the market--he could have been charging $100 or $1,000 for a bottle of water and it wouldn't make any difference to whether a truck could get over a washed-out highway and into the disaster zone.
The only actual solution to a shock like this is decisive government action to resolve those bottlenecks--to fix the infrastructure and get the essentials moving again. To respond to such a crisis with "let the market work, suppliers will come" is not just cruel--it's _stupid_. It's kindergarten-level magical thinking, dressed up as hardnosed realism. _Anti-Fascist Economics_ treats these idiots with the derision they deserve. We should, too.

I just got home from Operation Epic Fury in the Middle East. I saw a lot while overseas. And I've seen a lot since coming home. This is a bit of a long story but it would mean the world to me if you would take a few minutes to hear it.
_When I found out we were deploying, I told my wife on the couch after the kids were asleep._
I told my 7-year-old in the garage one Sunday after church. I said I was going far away. To a desert. That I'd call. That I wouldn't be home for a while. She asked how long. She was in 1st grade. I said she'd already be in 2nd grade by the time I got back.
**That 's forever to a 7-year-old.**
I barely told the little ones. My 3-year-old didn't understand until I'd been gone for a week. Then he cried himself to sleep asking for me. Night after night. For months. Boys just need their dads. There is nothing in the world like hearing that from a war zone and not being able to walk down the hall.
The hardest thing for me while over there wasn't the unending missile strikes.
It was a Saturday in August. My middle girl turned 5. They threw her a pool party. I FaceTimed in. Somebody turned the phone around. Her face lit up.
**I hung up so I wouldn 't cry in front of her.**
I prayed one verse more times than I can count. Deuteronomy 31.
**Do not fear, for I go with you.**
I prayed it in the job I was sent to do. I prayed it when I couldn't do a thing about a little boy asking for his dad.
**I 'm home now.**

The girls ran at the truck. My son hugged me and then treated me like a stranger for two days. Now he will not leave my side. Room to room. Everywhere I go.
My 7-year-old is different. Any time the house gets quiet -- any time she hears me and Rina talking low -- she runs in. Daddy, are you leaving again? Are you getting on a plane?
_I can 't just say no. Not all the way. She knows it. I know it. That's what serving costs._
Some of the men I served with lived a harder version of that deployment than I did. Sand in everything they owned. Ninety seconds to a bunker that wouldn't save them from a direct hit. Then back on the line. I made it home. I'm asking you to say a prayer for them before you do anything else.
**[But now I need to ask you for one more favor.](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/QxNzo-z-v4QpWrj5HSPbKqfC-ss8iXbiUD3Xp2j_-dLlc5Xp79RI4exsMu8GTz80hFy33xHs_0nj3uMSrqhDs7nvu4aX9Vj-FBbDPqgAzgSPZVLeRQhF6Pdya6UZ_i8U44iZrnYVFLeYPZkyLEZ3O1TIswm0NLXd3Nt-9ZJi0ecLWPsG5sJpc4tKIvwnh8PX5-A3cIim9gxLadWNlKyGVwAkEqSCeNs1STpZXEPbVCu7bxBAWWFqSsYeVeh5FyC8b_UIQ9f2r-PwuZfOJGmk_CqtNw8IFqYVeCICr3Qc7nkw3SR6tSKfeSj6tu668UhGSvojZ7kcA-Np2ziLuIHK8XlKfZN8Bzg6eYc0Ie1XCxrSziwuedIGXUFqYAVGvodL2xTRMcSUbBGR2sHGmuWF0tJa-oMXaczj0xpWDJWd3Vaz5SRFT-W-aZGxnfwl_7A2gO947DsadC76y_m_6KgQdk9Qo6NXJMYz60AkJBt_oDuvDkYciTBm5lA6gGC_mjySHyzWg74bmwZLSUZogJPuJ3s_Rtc-qjYL0KxLyASx6UTRgbSX6yCFhZvPCo9F4CznF7Px12Jniyc8QHWlV_Bg4X9HiyW12ltgS2QVjoEuy-5NktYHZiJIS5guIDBm0dTJ6AaGSjr7B4nsimW0AeGpzE6hFTEphQ7jMbNJ1AivjDEJEEo8QUYHw62DLwQV6RqypMgh_sMR_lvmk1IoQCZxQi78WAIHd05dM9VQF91mFQvKRVWJDis_nlktO4p_38dJXrK4DPjsBcNfBTI22msMX2H08gzyy_lsJL9afohYydsWDpCzM3oaR-ib-cAPiNVKKw_LiXGrZMp4h18l/t_RLmLe5p2WZVh8J4wUiec2praThHZuJ/26)**
When I came home, I looked at the country we'd been sent to defend.
Hasan Piker is on the air saying America deserved 9/11. That we're worse than Al Qaeda. Socialists are calling this a terrible country.
The soldiers I served with still have sand in their clothes. I hung up on my daughter's fifth birthday so I wouldn't cry in front of her.
**_That 's the country they're running down._**

clean_body: This is what serving our nation costs. | I just got home from Operation Epic Fury in the Middle East. I saw a lot while overseas. And I've seen a lot since coming home. This is a bit of a long story but it would mean the world to me if you would take a few minutes to hear it. When I found out we were deploying, I told my wife on the couch after the kids were asleep. I told my 7-year-old in the garage one Sunday after church. I said I was going far away. To a desert. That I'd call. That I wouldn't be home for a while. She asked how long. She was in 1st grade. I said she'd already be in 2nd grade by the time I got back. That 's forever to a 7-year-old. I barely told the little ones. My 3-year-old didn't understand until I'd been gone for a week. Then he cried himself to sleep asking for me. Night after night. For months. Boys just need their dads. There is nothing in the world like hearing that from a war zone and not being able to walk down the hall. The hardest thing for me while over there wasn't the unending missile strikes. It was a Saturday in August. My middle girl turned 5. They threw her a pool party. I FaceTimed in. Somebody turned the phone around. Her face lit up. I hung up so I wouldn 't cry in front of her. I prayed one verse more times than I can count. Deuteronomy 31. Do not fear, for I go with you. I prayed it in the job I was sent to do. I prayed it when I couldn't do a thing about a little boy asking for his dad. I 'm home now. The girls ran at the truck. My son hugged me and then treated me like a stranger for two days. Now he will not leave my side. Room to room. Everywhere I go. My 7-year-old is different. Any time the house gets quiet -- any time she hears me and Rina talking low -- she runs in. Daddy, are you leaving again? Are you getting on a plane? I can 't just say no. Not all the way. She knows it. I know it. That's what serving costs. Some of the men I served with lived a harder version of that deployment than I did. Sand in everything they owned. Ninety seconds to a bunker that wouldn't save them from a direct hit. Then back on the line. I made it home. I'm asking you to say a prayer for them before you do anything else. When I came home, I looked at the country we'd been sent to defend. Hasan Piker is on the air saying America deserved 9/11. That we're worse than Al Qaeda. Socialists are calling this a terrible country. The soldiers I served with still have sand in their clothes. | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. **You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does.** And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.**This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood.** It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. [**And God brought us the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=0c56e60350fd444196a9ea326796d401&_e=eaEoe79IQrQVcK454myPhW6Q24ZHrLQbgbqj4IzlJ6h23-Pj7QVPVSjYgJC2Ysgt77ZQATGlin8m3Unq_CohKc8zGujuqGsORm6qbJJ24p5-r0EMamDOhFuyPfYNaiCG7oDU0rHi7watDkn9FfOYNx1C9FPgrtwmhjHoa5rIraNR5LesHGLbn7Y3W1UrcnAtvqxuZh5ouWe-6I-x3k_nCQK-L0YsxOir0bavNxEZDzP2v4HuCvIGeKNmkYmjVWZVp8Xn8sMR6bJjniGJ2cnK6VGoiNO4KiuXnDSVLvQrUcYh7KpYTkfMMZ86nt7TbbXXLY56bZKA3o2QvRF0Ii9d1wWtvCilszRHtZizB1t9EfvUHTrHr8haa222EfY5WebaxCioe57MXrmBEwL6P2N5xKaZKHtKCkE-HwUyBdnhkoN7_-rVHIMA8IfCTHEDF8Jx-NfrqCYnPCEOOW-TqCGPJbtdLJrrlLqhssY6b0weDgK8MJ2bZBVl2zW1rLSJvrS9kbbCG1pzV4cv18N8X_quLQVFhiaS_RZLwxStb2jS8HZ0A1gfAtVmgV7OXr0PVF7vrWZt-iKQ-j2PCQ7Jb_VvGMQsmkKXFLQ5Sob5Ohsi8hXkE7m1E862cIeoBzc5d3nAj55SbGFKS55azIURz2eT2Kgr6zfmhTIMyR8O2pkilZGan-wxcOM1oIdrlAY1zD_MqXHdQBF-lB3knEtnjKccO4kteOTEJ90l9IDjYSqPmngzXRtlVGnevhFd76hDnkQ0Oe17ngX-vdVqE3twSumUNRvAAxVEnTfrcWIk08mX4EFE8t8I1eEN8Nx6IIk1h6F8-vobfYVWVi0eKm847BPiZcWa3FKnXQZ5HmhSe2ABMUuVNXIBmxnuICVI_SK7nvEJ4oVWo8E1bxrZ79HfDK4K64SB3RCBiGuEXUbq5W9bwJ4uuF0jckcfY80CIqFi_pj6L1FaLdcmn54OIn1tsGg8a0hSnLWMmoERWqVfQyNzPEk7EX3srEJmnb_x0EVKvPTWWNAo-9roAZMSw6QyGPbLtQ%3D%3D) You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. clean_body: You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer. | | | | Dear Peter,I know you and I have never met. But I’m writing to you today because I’m desperate. | | | This is Erik, me, and our three children in the family photo.I wish I didn’t have to blur our faces. But with the death threats we’ve been getting, I couldn’t afford to take any chances.I should explain...You’ve heard about Erik on the news.He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer who was speeding a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk. | | | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does. And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood. It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. Thanks to kind-hearted people like you, they get these officers the lawyers and expert witnesses they need to fight back against activist prosecutors and judges......and win.Peter, you’ve already read my email this far, so I’m going to come right out and ask: I know it’s strange to ask for your support in the very first email I’ve ever written you.But we have nowhere else to turn.Erik and I come from working-class families.We’re not wealthy.And with Erik being found guilty, we lost his salary and our medical benefits. We’re barely getting by as it is. because LELDF is a nonprofit, your gift is tax-deductible too.But whatever God is prompting you to give, please act quickly.Erik’s legal team needs to be working around the clock on this appeal.Because if we don’t fight this injustice, Erik will be imprisoned. And you know how police officers are treated in prison. And when you access the secure donation page, you’ll see there is a box where you can type a message— If you’re a believer like Erik, maybe you could write a short prayer. I know it will mean the world to him. Peter, for the past three years Erik told me something over and over again: “It’s not about the hardships. It’s about the people God sends into your life during difficult times to help you.” I pray that today you’ll be one of those people God uses to help our family.Thank you, and God bless you.Sincerely, Cynthia Duran P.S. My husband doesn’t deserve this. He’s a decorated police officer who spent his entire career serving and protecting his city. That day in the park, he saved lives. And for that, Letitia James wants him locked up for NINE YEARS.Please don’t let the cop-haters destroy another good man. | | | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. Hey friends,Tennessee wants to build more youth prisons, and I wanted to know why. So I sat down with Zoe Jamail, Policy and Advocacy Director at the [Raphah Institute](https://us.list-manage.com/1BsGw0vQmV1?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), a Nashville nonprofit working to stop harm from spreading through communities and to move us away from locking people up as the first answer.
[**[BUTTON: LISTEN NOW**]](https://us.list-manage.com/m4ZrSGIkz1k?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)****

We talk about the years of investigative reporting on Tennessee’s juvenile facilities, why “more beds” isn’t the fix, and what works instead, from prevention to restorative justice to a free counseling program in Colorado that I’d love to see here.Zoe also shares what she thinks the legislature should do on transparency and oversight. TODAY'S TOP STORIES

PROPOSITION 137: VOTERS APPROVED $175 MILLION LAWMAKERS DO NOT HAVE TO
SPEND
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado voters agreed Tuesday to send $175 million a year to
conservation and wildfire work without raising a single tax rate. The
money still has to come from somewhere. In years the state collects
more than the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights lets it keep, it comes out
of what would have been refunded.

Lawmakers are not bound to spend it.

Proposition 137 passed with 51.88 percent, 1,347,245 to 1,249,749, a
margin of 97,496 in the Secretary of State‘s count last updated at
6:10 p.m. MST Saturday. The Associated Press called it approved at
10:12 a.m. MST Friday.

Only two measures on the ballot finished with a narrower vote margin.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

AMENDMENT 87: COLORADO’S FLAT INCOME TAX IS GONE AFTER 39 YEARS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Voters narrowly ended Colorado’s 39-year flat income tax, replacing
it with six brackets that will hit high earners hard while a companion
cap measure meant to stop it failed._

*
TOP EARNERS FACE STEEP INCREASES: The new brackets run from 3.71% up
to 8.41% above $1 million, and Legislative Council Staff estimates the
roughly 46,000 taxpayers earning $1 million or more will see an
average increase of $26,085 each.

*
NO INFLATION PROTECTION BUILT IN: Unlike federal brackets,
Colorado’s new rates won’t adjust for inflation, meaning the Blue
Book itself warns “more of taxpayers’ incomes will fall into the
higher brackets over time” unless the legislature or voters act
again.

*
PASSED BY A RAZOR-THIN MARGIN UNDER A LOWER BAR: Amendment 87 won with
just 51.37%, needing only a simple majority rather than the 55%
required of six other amendments, all of which failed, while a
competing measure to cap the tax rate also failed.

FREE

BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 9

_There is a danger to the American republic far more consequential
than the outcome of any election, the ambitions of any political
party, or the failures of any administration. It is the gradual
deterioration of the moral and intellectual character upon which
self-government depends._

_A wall has fallen in Texas. In Kansas, Nebraska, South Carolina and
Maine. This wall did not fall as the result of a sudden assault or
storm. This wall fell due to lack of maintenance. No one was
overseeing or inspecting the wall. Its foundation was crumbling. And
those who should have noticed and done something to repair and
strengthen the wall...did nothing._
__

subject: After the midterm results, the GOP is handing the reins to YOU
body:
How should we move forward?
| Friend,
---
There’s no way to sugarcoat it...
---
_The midterm election results were nothing short of shocking._
---
There’s going to be a lot of debate, discussion, and finger-pointing about what happened and why it happened in the coming days and weeks.
---
**But the first step is obvious to everyone: Our Party needs to focus on one thing above all else moving forward...**
---
**We MUST have a better ear for what matters most to _YOU_ – the loyal grassroots patriots who are the backbone of MAGA.**
---

name: Governor-elect Eric Barlow
subject: Governor-elect Eric Barlow Announces Senior Leadership Selections
body:
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M73NFTXWZ4DZQNVT2WVP6EYD_0)
---
| **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** November 10, 2026**Governor-elect Eric Barlow Announces Senior Leadership Selections** _Erin Taylor named Chief of Staff, Walter Eggers selected as Attorney General nominee, and Eydie Trautwein named Chief Operating Officer_**CHEYENNE, Wyoming** — Governor-elect Eric Barlow today announced three senior leadership selections for his incoming administration: Erin Taylor as Chief of Staff, Walter Eggers as his nominee for Attorney General, and Eydie Trautwein as Chief Operating Officer.The selections bring together experience in public policy, law and state government operations as Barlow prepares to take office. Eggers’ appointment as Attorney General will be subject to Wyoming Senate confirmation.“Wyoming deserves a government that listens, spends responsibly and delivers dependable service,” Governor-elect Barlow said. “Erin, Walter and Eydie understand our state and bring the experience and judgment needed to help lead this work. I will count on them to build strong relationships, address problems directly and keep our administration focused on serving the people of Wyoming.”Taylor brings more than 25 years of public policy experience at the federal, state and local levels. As Chief of Staff, she will lead the governor’s staff, alongside the Chief Operating Officer, and help coordinate the administration’s priorities with legislators, state agencies and communities.Taylor founded Taylor Strategies & Consulting in 2014 after serving eight years as executive director of the Wyoming Taxpayers Association. Her background includes energy and regulatory policy, business advocacy and association leadership. She also served as statewide campaign manager for U.S. Senator Mike Enzi’s 2014 primary campaign and as executive director of the Wyoming Association of Community College Trustees.A two-time University of Wyoming graduate, Taylor holds a bachelor’s degree in economics and a master’s degree in regulatory and environmental economics. Her community leadership has included chairing the Wyoming Business Alliance, serving on the Wyoming Community Foundation board, and gubernatorial appointments to the Wyoming Arts Council and Wyoming Lottery Corporation.Eggers brings extensive legal and management experience to his selection as Attorney General. Raised in Laramie, he graduated from American University in 1992 and the University of Wyoming College of Law in 1997. He began his career in Cheyenne, practicing as both a prosecutor and defense attorney before joining Holland & Hart in 2000.A partner from 2008 to 2024, Eggers led the firm’s Cheyenne office and later its Energy, Environment and Natural Resources Practice Group, overseeing more than 100 lawyers and legal professionals. His practice included administrative law, state and local taxation, litigation and appeals. Since 2025, he has taught professional responsibility, evidence, and oil and gas law at the University of Wyoming College of Law.Eggers has also devoted substantial time to expanding access to civil legal assistance. His service includes the Wyoming Access to Justice Commission and Equal Justice Wyoming. His professional and community contributions have earned recognition, including the Wyoming State Bar’s John M. Burman Extraordinary Service Award.Trautwein brings experience in state administration, legal services and coordination across government. As Chief Operating Officer, she will help oversee the governor’s office operations and support implementation of the administration’s priorities.Trautwein has served as Wyoming’s Deputy State Auditor, with experience supporting statewide financial and administrative systems. Her work has included coordinating a major upgrade of the state’s financial, human resources and payroll systems. She previously served as Director of Legal Resources and Judicial Education for the Wyoming Supreme Court, supporting judicial training and court improvement efforts.Individuals interested in serving in the Barlow Administration or learning more about the transition are encouraged to visit the governor-elect’s website at [governor-elect.wyo.gov.](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M73NFTXWZ4DZQNVT2WVP6EYD_1)**Media Contact:** Jessica JaubertCommunications DirectorOffice of Governor-elect Eric Barlow307-203-6288[governor-elect.wyo.gov](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M73NFTXWZ4DZQNVT2WVP6EYD_2)

_Hakeem as a kid growing up in Brooklyn_
[His brother Hasan] recalled them having a “little breakdance crew” and said his older brother had “notebooks with rap lyrics that he is penning.”
Jeffries also found escape in sports, especially his beloved Yankees and Knicks. The brothers played little league baseball. [They transformed their backyard into what Hasan described as a “multi-sports complex,” with their dad using leftover construction scraps to build a basketball hoop.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143246875/659567155/-1002985911?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZWU0NjBhMC00ZGRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xiVgpzX1RtpCzZiQ11cHZHzZKDjnvcO-8kN_fEVTPBE=&emci=f38720cb-37dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=9ee460a0-4ddd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=21290350)
The backyard was one outlet. Religion was another. The nearby Cornerstone Baptist Church was a pillar of family life in the Jeffries household.
Cornerstone’s senior pastor Lawrence Aker III told MS NOW that the church was where Jeffries “learned how to give speeches.”
“This is where he learned how to lead,” Aker said. “He led other youth ministries right here in this community.”
[A PASSION FOR SERVING OTHERS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143246876/659567156/-1002985911?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZWU0NjBhMC00ZGRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xiVgpzX1RtpCzZiQ11cHZHzZKDjnvcO-8kN_fEVTPBE=&emci=f38720cb-37dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=9ee460a0-4ddd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=21290350)

Hakeem loves local Brooklyn artists, including Biggie Smalls. | Hakeem as a kid growing up in Brooklyn [His brother Hasan] recalled them having a “little breakdance crew” and said his older brother had “notebooks with rap lyrics that he is penning.” Jeffries also found escape in sports, especially his beloved Yankees and Knicks. The brothers played little league baseball. The backyard was one outlet. Religion was another. The nearby Cornerstone Baptist Church was a pillar of family life in the Jeffries household. Cornerstone’s senior pastor Lawrence Aker III told MS NOW that the church was where Jeffries “learned how to give speeches.” “This is where he learned how to lead,” Aker said. “He led other youth ministries right here in this community.” (via MS NOW) His parents, a social worker and a substance abuse counselor, had one main expectation for their two sons: they had to get an advanced degree and then use what they learned to serve other people. Jeffries took the law school route, graduating from NYU in 1997. | His younger brother, now a professor of history at The Ohio State University, told MS NOW the two shared a bedroom through high school. And they often debated each other well into the night. “He enjoys a good intellectual joust, right?” Hasan said of his brother. “As we’re growing up, it’s sports. But once we got to sort of high school, it begins to shift, and we’re thinking more about the world. We’re talking about Malcolm X, we’re talking about Dr. King.” Hasan says politics began to infuse the conversation. (via MS NOW) Jeffries first entered politics after a brief stint in corporate law. He lost two bids for the New York State Assembly before winning on his third try. | Six years later in 2012, he was elected to Congress and landed a spot on the influential House Judiciary Committee. The panel helped lay the groundwork for Jeffries’ future high profile efforts, including working with the first Trump White House to pass the first major criminal justice reforms in roughly a decade, a bipartisan accomplishment that would later stand in contrast to his role as an impeachment manager. It’s a duality that Jeffries will now likely have to balance again as Democrats pledge to work legislatively to lower costs while at the same time holding the second Trump administration accountable. In his interview with MS NOW, Jeffries insisted the two goals are not mutually exclusive. (via MS NOW) When longtime House Democratic leader Nancy Pelosi, whom Jeffries has likened to a living legend, announced she would step away from leadership in 2022 to make way for a new generation, Jeffries was elected to replace her unopposed. (via MS NOW) After Democrats made historic gains in the House and Senate last week, Rep. Hakeem Jeffries made it official. The New Yorker formally announced he was running for speaker... For Jeffries, the speakership would be the fulfillment of a dream years in the making. He would become the first Black person to hold the job, capping a political ascent that has carried him from Brooklyn to the top of the Democratic Caucus. The 56-year-old will have to hold President Donald Trump accountable, as Democratic voters are demanding, while avoiding the kind of overreach that could alienate swing voters. He will also have to find ways to work with Trump and deliver legislative results on issues such as the high cost of living, even as he draws sharp contrasts with the president and Republicans ahead of the 2028 elections. Even his position is a paradox. He would be leading the largest Democratic House majority in more than 30 years, but Democrats will largely be acting as an opposition party to Trump for the next two years. (via MS NOW) In this moment of uncertainty, one thing is certain, though. | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. **You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does.** And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.**This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood.** It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. [**And God brought us the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund.**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=470ee7889b2f4fbc9d8ea3e24b1ff93b&_e=xXQOwHzb3nmNL8P08KMqaZHKRGupMqF4WyjM1HuZz8SaRDoXCN3J5iKfCfejTVzv-jtKT4kNaOVJH4d1uuSbmjyKgYZBqi4YNyNoS_79KRwgy_xnnd7yokZAhbXkR5e0nnbIOC6joIJ_Xg2dEcfnpJpLG4RVx1MRlfIRWBtIQ3Zxmu8DvENCa-jPL8T6Ou8HWYIM0f5ZCw-PrFIW9mu8qq30oMLNCDWTPSHgN5B29WZykSG_0nLhDCMYR0-UaxcYLszHy7IpQFI5eikm-2pnuRJcdgAa79PLT7ajLN-S6aST6L481bGqMlA_S4ULcfrfkXNLQR3U_s1N3LhElXndpsSXGuAgU27lpJk-u9yGelbRtci4M4022fIOzytP63N4NBTSCFh8i0jRot6D5YIkiA3qy1W0x6Ztzle8dAVG7WnVr19NP0dgJmSDYweu1Mg9nwRBfEpMUKj69BC-3WOqW3VQWBkR1mE7OYZcEfx24GTI5QW7g2DvvUOdYxf_g9HIRDd3eci_BHMKp9_BkKYNRayivRL-Hut4zkwXMtZbj-Daruiwiys0uCm5r2R1JZkcEwrx_r2ca_NiVA67gVqlEcsa0-YuZv4s0Wiefh3zvKnbqRD_XMog1m9dpXjeYV7VeS0WEZ-ypwBRp9DjIW-KKq0I2i_KmZvUp_1k9_Du94HUgTOGzLqzKajZKusyik_edJc1yvKZ2h09m0W2B8gO57_sKzPHIbu8p2C3fu3tzn4IrpLd_ohKM1VIOebzKVM4dfCEPoSat5BfS7wtMS8UQbUesLrm-VgbWxtt-jTRoSxS4aqobDLjhE5bhBsFhWHt1e62Of3TL1OTawC5V57J1T6rMu0fOfFAt4r4kNlDYrmTrJwtEluEEqQ9Bxb3o_E6QHLMZR9jhg4xoWSgR9kg3zNglxpbLg8cD_9viqZObUqPWZHY6WpwD0LbAACfSYJHuQYL-jVnP1SGLt6A2mvcyQ%3D%3D) You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. clean_body: You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer. | | | | Dear Friend,I know you and I have never met. But I’m writing to you today because I’m desperate. | | | This is Erik, me, and our three children in the family photo.I wish I didn’t have to blur our faces. But with the death threats we’ve been getting, I couldn’t afford to take any chances.I should explain...You’ve heard about Erik on the news.He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer who was speeding a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk. | | | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does. And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood. It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. Thanks to kind-hearted people like you, they get these officers the lawyers and expert witnesses they need to fight back against activist prosecutors and judges......and win.Friend, you’ve already read my email this far, so I’m going to come right out and ask: I know it’s strange to ask for your support in the very first email I’ve ever written you.But we have nowhere else to turn.Erik and I come from working-class families.We’re not wealthy.And with Erik being found guilty, we lost his salary and our medical benefits. We’re barely getting by as it is. because LELDF is a nonprofit, your gift is tax-deductible too.But whatever God is prompting you to give, please act quickly.Erik’s legal team needs to be working around the clock on this appeal.Because if we don’t fight this injustice, Erik will be imprisoned. And you know how police officers are treated in prison. And when you access the secure donation page, you’ll see there is a box where you can type a message— If you’re a believer like Erik, maybe you could write a short prayer. I know it will mean the world to him. Friend, for the past three years Erik told me something over and over again: “It’s not about the hardships. It’s about the people God sends into your life during difficult times to help you.” I pray that today you’ll be one of those people God uses to help our family.Thank you, and God bless you.Sincerely, Cynthia Duran P.S. My husband doesn’t deserve this. He’s a decorated police officer who spent his entire career serving and protecting his city. That day in the park, he saved lives. And for that, Letitia James wants him locked up for NINE YEARS.Please don’t let the cop-haters destroy another good man. | | | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. Out of every ballot cast across the whole state, it comes down to a few hundred. That’s not a lead. _That’s a coin flip._ Here’s what makes my blood boil: Democrats played a dirty trick in this race. Now only hundreds of votes separate them. | | | | Friend, Right now, just hundreds of votes separate Senator Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola. Out of every ballot cast across the whole state, it comes down to a few hundred. That’s not a lead. That’s a coin flip. Here’s what makes my blood boil: Democrats played a dirty trick in this race. They recruited a second “Dan Sullivan” to get on the ballot, a fake candidate with the same name with ties to the Democrats meant to confuse voters and pull votes away from the real one. And it worked well enough to matter. If the fake weren’t in this race, Dan would be leading right now. I knew what they were up to. That’s why I got on a plane and went to Alaska to campaign for Dan BEFORE Election Day. | But a race this close doesn’t end on Election Night. Every remaining ballot has to be counted, and every vote must be protected. You can bet Democrats will throw everything they have at this count, because they know this seat is within their reach. Make no mistake about what’s at stake. If Mary Peltola wins, she’ll vote with Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren. Dan Sullivan will stand up for our conservative values: secure borders, a strong military, and Alaska’s energy and jobs. We cannot afford to lose one more conservative voice in the Senate. Certainly not to a trick like this. For America, Ted Cruz | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

_**CONCORD, N.H. —** Today, the newly elected members of the New Hampshire House of Representatives voted to elect Representative Jason Osborne as Minority Leader for the upcoming two-year legislative session. New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement:_
“Congratulations to Representative Jason Osborne, our newly elected Minority Leader,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “This is an important opportunity to bring our caucus together, ensure Republican voters have a strong voice in the State House, and hold Democrats accountable for their actions.”
“The work ahead is about building momentum for a New Hampshire comeback. We must remain united, stand firm on our principles, and continue fighting for the Granite Staters who put their trust in us. I look forward to working alongside our House leadership and members as we work to earn back the majority.”
